If their pronoun is masculine the number is made feminine, and if it is feminine it is made masculine. So you say with the generic noun «ثلاثة من الغنم عندي», with the tāʾ in thalātha, because you say «غنم كثير» with the masculine for the pronoun latent in kathīr. The author of al-Miṣbāḥ related that with ghanam its pronoun may be masculine or feminine. And «ثلاث من البط», omitting the tāʾ from thalāth, because you say «بط كثيرة» with the feminine for the pronoun latent in kathīr. And «ثلاثة» or «ثلاث من البقر», because the pronoun of baqar may be masculine or feminine, since there are two usages for baqar, masculine and feminine. Allah the Exalted said: «إن البقر تشابه علينا» with a masculine pronoun, and it was read «تشابهت» with it feminine. As for the collective noun, its rule is that of the masculine if it is for rational beings, like al-qawm, al-rahṭ and al-nafar, and if it is for non-rational beings its rule is that of the feminine, like al-jāmil (a herd of camels) and al-bāqir (a herd of cattle). This is what the grammarians mentioned, but there is a reservation about it, because niswa is a collective noun and its rule is that of the feminine by agreement, so one says «ثلاث نسوة».
Masculine and feminine with a plural are reckoned by the state of its singular: if its singular is masculine its number is made feminine, and if it is feminine its number is made masculine. Therefore you say «ثلاثة اصطبلات», plural of iṣṭabl with a disjunctive hamza with kasra, and «ثلاثة حمامات», because al-iṣṭabl and al-ḥammām are masculine; and you say «ثلاث سحابات», omitting the tāʾ, by reference to saḥāba, which is feminine. Of the state of the singular, the state of its wording is not taken into account, such that one would say «ثلاث طلحات» omitting the tāʾ; nor is the state of its meaning taken into account, such that one would say «ثلاث أشخص», likewise omitting it, meaning women, since shakhṣ applies to male and female; rather one looks at what the singular is entitled to with respect to its pronoun, and reverses its rule in the number. As for the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فكان مجني دون من كنت أتقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three figures: two full-breasted girls and a girl come of age.)
it is poetic licence; the rule would have been «ثلاثة شخوص» with the tāʾ, but he alluded to women by al-shukhūṣ, and what made that easy was his words «كاعبان ومعصر», so the wording was joined to what supports the intended meaning, namely the feminine. Al-kāʿib is the girl when her breasts begin to swell, and al-muʿṣir, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ṣād, is the girl when she first reaches maturity, called that because she has entered the age (ʿaṣr) of youth, as al-Khalīl said.
Furthermore, the reins of speech have run away with us, so what has preceded is sufficient for us; we have brought it for its importance and benefit, and whoever wants more must refer to the lengthy works.
2- Know that they have formed broken plurals of some nouns not on the singular in use; rather they took another word synonymous with it and formed the broken plural on what is not used. Among that is rahṭ and arāhiṭ. The poet said:
يا بؤس للحرب التي ... وضعت أراهط فاستراحوا
(Oh, the misery of war, which brought down noble clans, and they were at rest!)
It is not regular for rahṭ to be pluralised as arāhiṭ, because this form is among the plurals of the quadriliteral and what has its number of letters, like jaʿfar and jaʿāfir, jadwal and jadāwil, arnab and arānib. Arhuṭ is not the plural of rahṭ [Translator's note: as written; the sense of the argument appears to be that arāhiṭ is not the plural of arhuṭ]; for if it were so it would not be irregular. What shows that is that the poet brought it when he needed it, saying:
وفاضح مفتضح في أرهطه ... من أرفع الوادي ولا من بعثطه
(A disgracer, himself disgraced among his clans — not from the highest part of the valley, nor from its best ground.)
Al-buʿthuṭ and al-buʿthūṭ: the navel (centre) of the valley and the best place in it.
Furthermore, the grammarians differed over arāhiṭ: some of them claimed that it is the plural of arhuṭ, which is the plural of rahṭ, which is the group of three to ten; most of the grammarians claimed that arāhiṭ is the plural of rahṭ contrary to rule. The verse is the opening of an ode by Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn Ḍubayʿa ibn Qays ibn Thaʿlaba, grandfather of the poet Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd, and after it:
والحرب لا يبقى لجا ... حمها التخيل والمراح
إلا الفتى الصبار في النّ ... نجدات والفرس الوقاح
والنثرة الحصداء وال ... ... بيض المكلّل والرماح
وتساقط الأوشاظ والذّ ... نبات إذ جهد الفضاح والكر بعد الفر إذ ... كره التقدم وال
نطاح كشفت لهم عن ساقها ... وبدا من الشر الصراح
(In war, swagger and high spirits do not endure its blaze — only the young man patient in hardships and the hardy horse, the tightly-woven coat of mail, the crowned helmets and the spears; the hangers-on and the tail-ends fall away when disgrace presses hard, and there is wheeling back after flight when advancing and butting are loathed. It bared its shin to them, and sheer evil appeared.)
The word āyīn in the poetry of Abū Nuwās:
In the I'rab section there occurred the saying of Alexander, in which he says: "Stealing victory is not of the āyīn of kings." We would like to cite some verses of Abū Nuwās in which he used the word āyīn, and it came out light and graceful despite its strangeness. Abū Nuwās said, describing what happened to him at the monastery of Nahrādhān:
بدير نهراذان لي مجلس ... وملعب وسط بساتينه
رحت إليه ومعي قينة ... نزوره يوم سعانينه
بكلّ طلاب الهوى فاتك ... قد آثر الدنيا على دينه
حتى توافينا إلى مجلس ... تضحك ألوان رياحينه
والنرجس الغض لدى ورده ... والورد قد خفّ بنسرينه
وجيء بالدن على مرفع ... وخاتم العلج على طينه
وطاف بالكأس لنا شادن ... يدميه مس الكف من لينه
يكاد من اشراق خديه أن ... يختطف الابصار من دونه
فلم يزل يسقي ونلهو به ... ونأخذ القصف بآيينه حتى غدا السكران من سكره ... كالميت في بعض أحايينه
(At the monastery of Nahrādhān I have a sitting-place and a playground amid its gardens. I went to it with a singing-girl, visiting it on its Palm Sunday, with every reckless seeker of passion who has preferred this world to his religion, until we gathered at a sitting-place where the colours of its sweet herbs laugh, the fresh narcissus beside its roses, and the roses set off by their eglantine. The wine-jar was brought on a stand, the foreigner's seal upon its clay, and a fawn-like youth went round with the cup for us, whom the touch of a hand would make bleed for his softness; from the radiance of his cheeks he almost snatches away the sight of those before him. He kept pouring, and we kept amusing ourselves with him, taking our revelry according to its āyīn, until the drunkard from his drunkenness became at times like a dead man.)
So his words «نأخذ القصف بآيينه» mean: according to its customs, its rules and its conditions.

dervis-irab:54-58.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلُوطاً إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَتَأْتُونَ الْفاحِشَةَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to mention the fifth and last of the stories of the sūra. (لوطا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" or "We sent". If you make it "remember", (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to "remember"; and if you make it "We sent", (إذ) is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of (لوطا). The clause (قال) is in the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (لقومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قال). The hamza is for disapproving, rebuking interrogation; (تأتون) is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and (الفاحشة) is the direct object, and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). In (وأنتم) the wāw is circumstantial and (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (تبصرون) is the khabar (predicate) of (أنتم). What is meant is the sight of the heart, i.e. you know that it is an abomination and yet you do it. (أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجالَ شَهْوَةً مِنْ دُونِ النِّساءِ): the hamza is for disapproving, rebuking interrogation; the rebuke was repeated to add to the condemnation and declaring loathsome this hideous deed that contravenes the laws of nature. A discussion of these deviant sexual inclinations, the depth of whose ugliness cannot be reached, will come in the Benefits section. (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause (تأتون الرجال) is its khabar; (شهوة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or the object; (من دون النساء) is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the agent. (بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ and (قوم) the khabar; (تجهلون) is an adjective of (قوم). (فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا أَخْرِجُوا آلَ لُوطٍ مِنْ قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُناسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) is an incomplete past verb; (جواب قومه) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أن قالوا) is an interpreted maṣdar in the place of the nominative, the postponed noun of (كان). The clause (أخرجوا) is the object of saying; it is an imperative verb and its agent; (آل لوط) is the direct object; (من قريتكم) is attached to (أخرجوا). (إنهم) gives the reason for expelling them; (إن) and its noun, and (أناس) is its khabar, and the clause (يتطهرون) is an adjective, i.e. they keep themselves clean of this filthy act. (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْناها مِنَ الْغابِرِينَ): the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted, supplied element understood from the context, i.e. so Lot went out with his family from their land after he sensed their scheming, their plotting and their awaiting misfortunes for him. (أنجيناه) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (أهله) is conjoined to the hāʾ, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); (إلا) is a particle of exception and (امرأته) is the excepted; the clause (قدرناها) is a ḥāl; (قدرناها) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (من الغابرين) is attached to (قدرناها), i.e. those who remained in the punishment. (وَأَمْطَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَراً فَساءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أمطرنا) is a verb and its agent; (عليهم) is attached to (أمطرنا); (مطرا) is a direct object. In (فساء) the fāʾ is a conjunction and (ساء) is a past verb of blame, and (مطر المنذرين) is the agent.

* Benefits:
Narcissism and sexual deviance:
Modern philosophers trace the phenomena of deviance in the sexual instincts back to narcissism; therefore we must explain this narcissism as the psychoanalysts understand it.
The ancient Greeks gave the name Narcissus to a youth of legend, of surpassing beauty and bewitching charms, who captivated whoever saw him and, with his beauty and his vanity, brought misery to the hearts of bashful virgins; yet he paid them no heed and did not respond to their supplication. He continued thus until heaven resounded with the prayers of his lovers and their entreaties to the gods to turn them away from him or turn him away from them. Nemesis, goddess of retribution and requital, answered this prayer and decreed that he should be madly in love with himself and should meet from himself the misery that his lovers met from him. The tellers of the legends said: no sooner had he gone to drink from a clear spring than he glimpsed his image in its water, and stopped at it marvelling at its beauty; the enchantment distracted him from his affairs, and he did not leave his place, bent over the water to gaze his fill on that image and slake his thirst by looking at it; but looking only increased his longing and yearning, and longing only increased his emaciation and withering, until he perished. The water-nymphs went to look for his remains and found in his place nothing but a drooping narcissus gazing at the water, never raising its sight to the sky. So the narcissus is forever drooping, its eye open, never sated with looking at its reflection on the banks of streams and pools. There are other versions of this legend, depicting the echo, wariness and torpor, which do not depart from this gist and attach to the instincts or inclinations and sensations which the malady of narcissism comprises. For that reason the psychoanalysts chose it, and found no term more suitable for the symptoms of that psychological phenomenon, together with the term's ancient roots in the Greek language, which they choose for coining new names in the sciences. The first to introduce this term into psychological medicine was Dr. Havelock Ellis, the famous pioneer of sexual research; then the psychiatrists broadened the study of this malady, traced its symptoms and concomitants, and investigated which are its primary concomitants and which its secondary or derivative ones. Of its branches that relate to the study of deviants, two concern us here:
1- One of them is called auto-eroticism (self-desire).
2- The second of them is called self-idolisation.
Auto-eroticism predominates in physical cases accompanied by disorder of the sexual functions in the person concerned, and the disorder of these functions reaches the point that the afflicted person ejaculates if he looks long at his body naked in the mirror and the like, and that he desires his body as though it were the body of a person foreign to him; but it is a desire which the patient exaggerates.
Self-idolisation predominates in emotional and intellectual cases: the afflicted person takes himself as an idol which he worships, holds dear and pampers. So the concomitant of disguise and personification is indispensable in sexual deviance, which is a person's passionate love for himself from the side of lust. The deviant in loving his own sex or loving the other sex finds what he seeks and fulfils his aim; but the one who desires his own body is not able to fulfil his aim from it without contriving that by disguise and personification: he clothes his personality as another person whom he imagines to be himself or to take the place of himself, as the masturbator does when he puts a picture before himself.
Furthermore, it is useful for whoever longs to know the development of theories on sexual questions to refer to the books written on this subject; they shed light on the problem but do not solve it, because none of them has come to downplay the differences between the two sexes, nor to the claim of those who claim that the human being is bisexual, a mixture of masculinity and femininity by nature, and that sexual deviance in him is a general innate disposition that takes on its phases according to age from childhood to full growth in both sexes, as Freud and his followers say.
Abū Nuwās, who was one of the leading figures of the narcissists, depicted these phases in the best manner, as he frequented the places of study after this fashion according to his custom, in his words:
إذا ما وطئ الأمر ... د للعلم حصى المسجد
فقل حلّ لنا عقدا ... من الفقه واستفسد
فإن كان عروضيا ... فقولوا سجد الهدهد
وإن أعجبه النحو ... فها ذاك له أجود
وإن مال إلى الفقه ... فللفقه له أفسد
وان كان كلاميا ... فحرّك طرف المقود
وميله إلى الخير ... فقيه قرب ما يبعد وخذه كيفما شئت- اقتضابا أو على موعد وقل: هذا قضاء الله هل يدفع أو يجحد
(When a beardless youth treads the pebbles of the mosque in search of knowledge, say: "Untie for us a knot of jurisprudence", and seek to corrupt him. If he is a prosodist, say: "The hoopoe prostrated"; if grammar pleases him, that is better for him; if he inclines to jurisprudence, then jurisprudence is more corrupting for him; if he is a theologian, then tug the end of the halter; and incline him towards good, for in it is the nearness of what is far. Take him however you wish, on the spur of the moment or by appointment, and say: "This is Allah's decree — can it be repelled or denied?")
And he ended, speaking plainly:
فيا من وطئ المسجد ... من ذي بهجة أغيد
أنا قست على نفسي ... فهذا الأمر لا أجحد
(O you of radiant, supple youth who tread the mosque: I have judged by myself, and this matter I do not deny.)
We end this discussion; it was something necessary, even if this is not its place.
Correcting the transmission of a verse of Abū Nuwās in al-Kashshāf:
Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned in his Kashshāf, in the course of speaking about the people of Lot; he said:
«… They used to commit it in their assembly openly, not concealing themselves from one another, out of dissoluteness, shamelessness and immersion in sin; and it is as if Abū Nuwās built on their way his saying:
وبح باسم ما تأتي وذرني من الكنى ... فلا خير في اللذات من دونها ستر
(Openly name what you do, and leave me be of allusions; there is no good in pleasures behind a veil.)»
The correct transmission is «وبح باسم من تهوى ودعني من الكنى» ("Openly name the one you love, and spare me allusions") — the verse; and it is from a splendid ode whose beginning is:
ألا فاسقني خمرا وقل لي هي الخمر ... ولا تسقني سرا إذا أمكن الجهر
(Come, give me wine to drink and tell me "It is wine"; and do not give me to drink in secret when openness is possible.)
And after the verse:
فعيش الفتى في سكرة بعد سكرة ... فإن طال هذا عنده قصر العمر
(The young man's life is in one drunkenness after another; if this lasts long for him, life is shortened.)
And after it:
وما الغرم إلا أن تراني صاحيا ... وما الغرم إلا أن يتعتعني السكر
(The only loss is that you see me sober; the only gain [Translator's note: the source repeats «الغرم», "loss", in both hemistichs; the commonly transmitted second half reads «الغُنْم», "gain"] is that drunkenness makes me stagger.)
We do not pass you by without pausing at the first verse, for he said «وقل لي هي الخمر» ("and tell me: it is wine"). This may seem padding at first glance, but if the reader remembers that the human being has five senses, he will know that Abū Nuwās intended to bring in the sense of hearing, which remains deprived of the pleasure of wine while drinking it; so he asked his drinking-companion to address him with its name so as to include his sense of hearing. This is among the marvels of his acuteness.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(طس. تِلْكَ آياتُ الْقُرْآنِ وَكِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): the discussion of the i'rab and meaning of «طس» has preceded in the treatment of the opening letters of the sūras. «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «آيات القرآن» its khabar (predicate); «كتاب مبين» is conjoined to «القرآن», and «مبين» is an adjective. The secret of the indefiniteness and the conjunction will come in the Rhetoric section.
(هُدىً وَبُشْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): «هدى» may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governing word being the demonstrative sense contained in «تلك», i.e., guiding [Translator's note: the source prints «هاديه», evidently for «هادية»] and giving glad tidings; and it may be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "it is guidance and glad tidings". The meaning of its being guidance for the believers, when they are already guided, is its increasing them in their guidance.
(الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ): «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «المؤمنين», and you may cut it off (qaṭʿ) as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "they are those who". The clause «يقيمون الصلاة» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», and the clause «يؤتون الزكاة» is conjoined to «يقيمون الصلاة». «وهم»: the wāw is of ḥāl, and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ, or the wāw is a conjunction; the clause «يوقنون» is its khabar. «بالآخرة» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يوقنون». The (second) «هم» is a mubtadaʾ brought in to separate between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is that it was repeated because «بالآخرة» separated the first «هم» from its khabar], so that it adjoins the khabar in form. The secret of the change in the arrangement will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ): resumptive speech, brought to explain the reason for their unbelief and their bewilderment and wavering in their deeds. «إن» and its noun; the clause «لا يؤمنون» is the ṣila of «الذين»; «بالآخرة» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يؤمنون»; the clause «زينا» is the khabar of «إن». «زينا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لهم» are attached to «زينا»; «أعمالهم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ is a conjunction; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يعمهون» its khabar, i.e., they are bewildered and waver between abandoning them, because they are clearly false and manifestly evil, and continuing in them. It has also been said that «يعمهون» means they continue without wavering, since the thought of giving them up never crossed their minds for a moment; this is fine and strong, but ʿamah, as al-Zamakhsharī and other authorities on the language say, is wavering and bewilderment, like the state of one who has lost the road. It is related of a certain Bedouin that he entered the market, never having seen it before, and said: "I saw the people ʿamihīn," meaning wavering in their activities and occupations. The lexicons almost agree that «العمه» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «عمه يعمه» and «يعمه», of the patterns of ḍaraba and fataḥa: ʿamahan, ʿumūhan, ʿumūhiyyatan and ʿamahānan, i.e., he was bewildered in his way or his affair and wavered in error; so he is ʿamih, plural ʿamihūn, and ʿāmih, plural ʿāmihūn and ʿummah.
(أُوْلئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذابِ وَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ): «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذين» its khabar; «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «سوء العذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila. «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «في الآخرة» are attached to «الأخسرون», and «الأخسرون» is its khabar; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ brought in to separate between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar so that it adjoins the khabar in form; its discussion has preceded. It must also be pointed out that His word «الأخسرون» may be in its proper sense of preference (tafḍīl), relative to the disbelievers, or it may be for intensification, not for sharing, because the believer has no loss at all in the Hereafter.
(وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ): the wāw is resumptive; «إن» and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause «تلقى» is its khabar. The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you), and «القرآن» is a second direct object. «من لدن» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تلقى»; «حكيم» is muḍāf ilayhi and «عليم» an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness:
As for indefiniteness: «الكتاب المبين» was made indefinite so as to be rendered vague by the indefiniteness and thereby more majestic; similar to it is «مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر». As for its being conjoined to «القرآن» although it is the Qur'an itself, that is of the kind of conjoining one of two attributes to the other, as when you say: "This is the deed of the generous one and the bountiful, noble one"; and also because the conjoined term contains an attribute additional to the concept of the term it is conjoined to.
2- Repetition of the pronoun:
In His words «وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون» the pronoun was repeated, so that the meaning of the speech became: none is certain of the Hereafter with true certainty except these who combine faith and righteous action, because fear of the Hereafter makes them bear hardships. We have mentioned before that placing the pronoun as a mubtadaʾ gives restriction (ḥaṣr), as in the words of the Exalted «هم ينشرون», whose meaning is "none raises the dead but they". As for the reason for its repetition here, it is that the original speech was «هم يوقنون بالآخرة»; then the genitive was placed before its governing word out of concern for it, and it came to separate the mubtadaʾ and the khabar. It was desired that the khabar follow directly on the mubtadaʾ, but the genitive had come between them, so its mention was refreshed (ṭurriya) so that the khabar would follow it [Translator's note: the source prints «فطري ذكره ليلية الخبر»; «ليليه» seems intended]; and the purpose of concern for the preposition and its genitive noun was not lost, since it remained fronted as it was. It is not objectionable for a word to be repeated, separated for its sake alone, after something that calls for refreshing it.
3- Expression by the nominal and the verbal clause:
We have said in places in this book that expression is sometimes by the nominal clause and sometimes by the verbal clause, and that this is not left to arbitrariness; one of the two expressions is chosen over the other for a kind of emphasis, intensification, continuity or discontinuity. Faith and certainty in the Hereafter are a fixed matter whose permanence is required, so He brought it as a nominal clause and made its khabar an imperfect verb, saying «وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون», to indicate that their certainty continues by way of constant renewal. As for performing the prayer and giving the zakāt, they are among the things that recur and are renewed at their appointed times, so He brought them as two verbs, saying «الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة».

* Benefits:
Imam al-Zamakhsharī raised a question on this matter based on his Muʿtazilite principle: «If you say: how did He attribute the adorning of their deeds to Himself, when He attributed it to Satan in His words "And Satan adorned for them their deeds"?» And he answered: «I say: between the two attributions there is a difference, namely that attributing it to Satan is literal (ḥaqīqa) and attributing it to Allah the Mighty and Majestic is figurative (majāz). It has two routes in the science of bayān. The first is that it be of the figurative usage called istiʿāra (metaphor); the second is that it be of the majāz ḥukmī (figurative attribution). The first route: when He gave them enjoyment through long life and ample provision, and they made Allah's favour to them in that and His beneficence toward them a means to following their lusts, their insolence, their preferring ease and luxury, and their aversion to the difficult obligations and wearisome hardships incumbent on them, it was as if He had adorned their deeds for them by that. The angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, alluded to this in His words "But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance." The second route: His giving Satan respite and leaving him free to adorn for them is an evident connection (mulābasa) with the adorning, so it was attributed to Him, because figurative attribution is validated by some connection. It has also been said that they are the good deeds which they were obliged to do: Allah adorned them for them, but they were blind to them and went astray; this is ascribed to al-Ḥasan.» [Translator's note: the source does not mark clearly where al-Zamakhsharī's quotation ends; it is closed here.]
The people of the Sunna answered that this answer is built on the corrupt principle of the obligation to observe what is good and best (al-ṣalāḥ wa-l-aṣlaḥ) and the impossibility of Allah the Exalted creating for the servant anything but what is in his interest; hence he made the adorning by Allah the Exalted figurative and by Satan literal. Had he reversed the answer, he would have attained what is right. Consider his inclination to the other interpretation — that the deeds of righteousness are meant — despite its remoteness, because it does not expose his principle to refutation. Moreover, adorning does occur concerning good, in the words of the Exalted «ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم», though most of its occurrences concern what is not righteousness, as in His words «زين للناس حب الشهوات», «زين للذين كفروا الحياة الدنيا» and «كذلك زين للمسرفين». What makes it unlikely that it be taken as deeds of righteousness is the annexation of the deeds to them in His word «أعمالهم»; deeds of righteousness are not annexed to them, because they never did them, and the apparent sense of the annexation gives that. Do you not see the words of the Exalted «ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم» and His words «قل لا تمنوا علي إسلامكم بل الله يمن عليكم أن هداكم للإيمان»? He left faith in both places unannexed to them, because it did not proceed from them, and annexed outward Islam to them, because it proceeded from them.

dervis-irab:59-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَدائِقَ): plural of ḥadīqa, i.e. a garden, from aḥdaqa bil-shayʾ, "it surrounded the thing". Since the garden is surrounded by walls it was called ḥadīqa; otherwise it is not called by that name. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-ḥadīqa is a garden with a wall around it, faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla, because the wall surrounds it (aḥdaqa bihā), i.e. encloses it; then they extended it until they applied ḥadīqa to a garden even without a wall; the plural is ḥadāʾiq.» In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «Al-ḥadīqa: every garden with a wall around it.» Among their sayings: «Your letter reached me, and I took my pleasure in the most delightful of its meadows and the splendour of its gardens.»

* I'rab:
(قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلامٌ عَلى عِبادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفى): resumptive speech, introduced to command His Messenger ﷺ to praise Him, the Exalted, and to send peace upon the chosen, the excellent ones of His creation. It is as if this praise were an elegant opening (barāʿat istihlāl) for the proofs and evidences He will present of the divine unity, knowledge and power, whose mention will come; and that is after He finished the stories of these five sūras [Translator's note: so in the source, «السور الخمس»; the context indicates the five stories of this sūra]. (قل) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you", i.e. O Muḥammad, so that it may be a model which every writer and orator follows and on whose pattern one proceeds in every beneficial science. (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (لله) its khabar (predicate); (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ, what permitted beginning with it [as an indefinite] being the meaning of supplication in it; (على عباده) is the khabar; (الذين) is an adjective of (عباده), and the clause (اصطفى) is the ṣila (relative clause), the referring pronoun being omitted, i.e. "He chose them"; they are the believers qualified for this world and the Hereafter. (آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): the hamza is for interrogation; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير) the khabar; (أم) is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun applying to their gods, and the clause (يشركون) is the ṣila. (أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ): (أم) is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), because its condition is lacking, namely the precedence of the interrogative hamza; it means (بل), and the digression is in the sense of silencing and rebuking. (من) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila; the khabar of (من) is omitted, its implied form being "better, or what they associate?", so what was stated in the first interrogation is supplied, relying on it. This is what al-Zamakhsharī chose, and it is fine and consistent with the speech. Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said:
«A balancing clause must be implied, and that implied clause has become like what is uttered because the import indicates it. The implied form of that clause is: "Is He who created the heavens and the earth like him who did not create?", and likewise its sisters. What was implied in these places has been made explicit elsewhere, as in the saying of the Exalted: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق.»
We see no clear difference between the two views. (أنزل) is conjoined to (خلق); (لكم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من السماء) is attached to (أنزل); (ماء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (أنبتنا) is conjoined to what precedes by way of iltifāt (shift of person), which will come in the Rhetoric section; (به) is attached to (أنبتنا); (حدائق) is the direct object and (ذات بهجة) is an adjective of (حدائق); what permitted its being singular is that the qualified noun is a plural of abundance for non-rational things.
(ما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُنْبِتُوا شَجَرَها): the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of (حدائق), or a ḥāl of it because it is specified by the adjective. (ما) is negative; (كان) is an incomplete past verb; (لكم) is the fronted khabar of (كان), and (أن) and what falls in its domain is its postponed noun; (تنبتوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by (أن), the wāw is the agent and (شجرها) is the object. (أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation containing the meaning of negation; (إله) is a mubtadaʾ, beginning with it being permitted because it conveys information on account of the interrogation; (مع الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar. (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) whose meaning is silencing; this expression is repeated five times, as you will see. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (قوم) the khabar, and the clause (يعدلون) is an adjective. (أَمَّنْ جَعَلَ الْأَرْضَ قَراراً وَجَعَلَ خِلالَها أَنْهاراً): the parsing of this construction has preceded, so draw the analogy with it. (قرارا) is the second object of (جعل); (وجعل خلالها أنهارا) is conjoined to the first clause. (خلالها) may be an adverb of (جعل) in the sense of "created", transitive to one object, or in the position of the second object, taking it in the sense of "made into"; on the first view (قرارا) is a ḥāl. [Translator's note: so in the source; on the first view it is presumably (أنهارا) in the second clause that would be the single object.] (وَجَعَلَ لَها رَواسِيَ): a conjoined clause. (وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ حاجِزاً أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is conjoined to what precedes, and its parsing has preceded.
(أَمَّنْ يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذا دَعاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ): its parsing has preceded; the clause (دعاه) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (المضطر) is a passive participle, and its ṭāʾ was originally the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form. (وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفاءَ الْأَرْضِ أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ): its parsing has preceded. (قليلا) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted time; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), to make the little less; (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb one of whose two tāʾs has been dropped, and the wāw is the agent. (أَمَّنْ يَهْدِيكُمْ فِي ظُلُماتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ): its parsing has preceded. (وَمَنْ يُرْسِلُ الرِّياحَ بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ تَعالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): its parsing has also preceded. (أَمَّنْ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَمَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ): its parsing has also preceded. (أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ قُلْ هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): (إن) is conditional and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then bring your proof". We have stated before that His saying «أإله» is mentioned five times: the first ends with His saying «بل هم يعدلون», the second with His saying «بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون», the third with His saying «قليلا ما يذكرون», the fourth with His saying «تعالى الله عما يشركون», and the fifth with His saying «قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين». [Translator's note: the source quotes the first as «بل هم يعدلون» and the third as «قليلا ما يذكرون»; the verses read «بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ» and «قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ».]

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person) in His words «فأنبتنا به حدائق ذات بهجة» after His words «أم من خلق السموات والأرض وأنزل لكم من السماء ماء»: in conveying the report He moved from the third person to the first person, speaking of Himself, in His words «فأنبتنا». The secret in it is to emphasise that the act of causing to grow belongs exclusively to Him, the Exalted, and to announce that causing the gardens of various kinds to grow, with what appears in them of embellishments of colours and beauties of forms, diverse tastes and different scents varying in the sweetness of their fragrance and perfume — all of that none is able to do except a powerful Creator, and He is Allah alone. Therefore He reinforced this exclusiveness by saying after that «ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها». Abū Nuwās grasped this truth and said:
تأمل في رياض الأرض وانظر ... إلى آثار ما صنع المليك
عيون من لجين شاخصات ... بأنظار هي الذهب السبيك
على قضب الزبرجد شاهدات ... بأن الله ليس له شريك
(Contemplate the meadows of the earth and look at the traces of what the Sovereign has made: eyes of silver, gazing with pupils that are molten gold, upon stems of chrysolite, bearing witness that Allah has no partner.)
Did Abū Nuwās repent?
Furthermore, perhaps you wonder at these verses brimming with deep faith and issuing from a man like Abū Nuwās. Those who accused him did not wrong him, nor did they lack proofs for accusing him of corruption; but they wronged philosophy, thinking it a path leading those acquainted with it to heresy (zandaqa) and its doctrines. There is no heresy here with Abū Nuwās, and no doctrine other than licentiousness and love of showing off. Ibrāhīm al-Naẓẓām was among the most learned of the people of his time in what they call the sciences of the ancients, and Abū Nuwās used to attend his lessons; he would forbid him from vulgarity and remind him of the threat [of punishment], saying to him: "Whoever looks forward to Allah's promise must beware of His threat." But he would not desist from his idle talk and licentiousness, until he despaired of him and expelled him from his circle. So he composed about him his ode which became famous as al-Ibrāhīmiyya, whose opening is famous and widely circulated:
دع عنك لومي فإن اللوم إغراء ... وداوني بالتي كانت هي الداء
(Leave off blaming me, for blame is an incitement, and cure me with that which was itself the disease.)
And in it he mocks al-Naẓẓām:
فقل لمن يدعي في العلم فلسفة ... حفظت شيئا وغابت عنك أشياء
لا تخطر العفو إن كنت امرأ حرجا ... فإن خطرك بالدين إزراء
(Say to him who claims philosophy in knowledge: you have memorised something and many things have escaped you. Do not bar pardon if you are a scrupulous man, for your barring it is a disparagement of religion.)
Abū Nuwās was nothing but a reckless libertine, and licentiousness in the custom of his milieu was wit. The emir Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad advised him to repent of licentiousness, and he said to him: "As for licentiousness, not everyone is able to be licentious; licentiousness is only wit, and in it I do not go beyond the bounds of good manners or exceed its measure. As for sins, in them I trust in the pardon of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the saying of the Exalted: «يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا»." Abū Nuwās picked up the errors of the Murjiʾa and their saying: «With faith, no sin at all, great or small, does harm; and with polytheism, no good deed at all is of benefit». He proclaimed that, and it appears that it beguiled him:
ترى عندنا ما يسخط الله كله ... من العمل المردي الفتى ما خلا الشركا
(You see with us all that angers Allah of the deeds that ruin a young man — except polytheism.)
Then he modified his theory somewhat and was content to say that grave sins do not place their doer among the unbelievers nor deprive him of hope in Allah's pardon; his saying on that is famous:
تكثر ما استطعت من الخطايا ... فإنك بالغ ربا غفورا
تعض ندامة كفيك مما ... تركت مخافة النار السرورا
(Commit as many sins as you can, for you will reach a forgiving Lord; you will bite your palms in regret for the joy you abandoned for fear of the Fire.)
And among that is his saying:
يا كبير الذنب عفو الله من ذنبك أكبر
(O you of great sin, Allah's pardon is greater than your sin.)
However, he repented in the last part of his life, and we may discern the sincerity of his repentance from his poems composed at that age close to the end. He said, acknowledging that he had delayed it until its time had passed:
دبّ فيّ الفناء سفلا وعلوا ... وأراني أموت عضوا فعضوا ذهبت شرّتي وجدة نفسي ... وتذكرت طاعة الله
نضوا ليس من ساعة مضت بي إلا ... نقصتني بمرها لي
جزوا لهف نفسي على ليال وأيا ... م سلكتهن لعبا
ولهوا قد أسأنا كل الإساءة يا ... رب فصفحا عنا إلهي وعفوا
(Decay has crept into me, below and above, and I see myself dying limb by limb. My fervour and my soul's vigour are gone, and I have remembered obedience to Allah, worn out. No hour passes me but by its passing it diminishes a part of me. Alas for the nights and days I spent in play and amusement! We have done every wrong, O Lord, so forgive us, my God, and pardon.)

dervis-irab:7-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آنَسْتُ): I perceived from afar. One says «آنست نارا» (I perceived a fire), «آنست فزعا» (I perceived alarm) and «آنست منه رشدا» (I perceived soundness of judgment in him); so it is used of the material and the abstract.
(بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ): it is read with annexation and without it, as will come in the I'rab. «الشهاب» is anything luminous generated from fire; also what is seen like a star that has darted down; also a star in general; also a spearhead, because of its glitter. Its plurals are «شهب», «شهبان», «شهبان» [Translator's note: so in the source, the same form printed twice; presumably shuhbān and shihbān] and «أشهب». One says "So-and-so is a shihāb of war" when he is keen in it. «القبس», with two fatḥas, is fire taken as a brand; you say: «خذ لي قبسا من النار» (take a brand of the fire for me), and «مقبسا» and «مقباسا»; «اقبس لي نارا» and «اقتبس». From it: "You are only like the hasty fire-taker (al-qābis al-ʿajlān)", i.e., the one taking a brand; "My visiting you is only like the hasty taking of a brand"; and you say: "I am only a brand from your fire and a handful from your traces." «قبسته نارا» and «أقبسته» (I gave him fire), as you say «بغيته الشيء» and «أبغيته». Figuratively: «قبسته علما وخبرا» (I gave him knowledge and news), and «أقبست».
(تَصْطَلُونَ): it contains substitution (ibdāl), because its original is «تصتلون»; when the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form came after a letter of covering (iṭbāq), namely the ṣād, it was changed to ṭāʾ according to the rule. It is from «صلي بالنار», with kasra on the lām. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «صلي بالنار and صليها, ṣalan, of the pattern of taʿiba: he felt its heat. Al-ṣilāʾ, on the pattern of kitāb, is the heat of the fire. صليت اللحم أصليه, of the pattern of ramā: I roasted it.» In al-Asās: «صلي النار and صلي بها; "يصلى النار الكبرى"; تصلّاها, تصلّى بها, أصلاه and صلّاه; and a شاة مصليّة is a roasted sheep, and I have roasted it.»
(جَانٌّ): a snake of light, quick movement. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj it says: «al-jānn is a collective noun for the jinn; also a snake with dark-rimmed eyes that does no harm, common in houses.» They said it is very large, even though it is light in speed of movement.
(وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): and did not come back. One says «عقب المقاتل» when the fighter turns back to attack after fleeing. The poet said:
فما عقبوا إذ قيل هل من معقب ... ولا نزلوا يوم الكريهة منزلا
(They did not turn back when it was asked, "Is there anyone to turn back?", nor did they take a stand on the day of battle.)
He describes a people as cowardly: if it was said, "Is there anyone who will turn back on his heels to the fight?", they did not return to it, nor did they take any position in it on the day of war. In al-Mukhtār: «You say: he turned his back in flight and did not «يعقب», with doubled and kasra-vowelled qāf, i.e., he did not turn round and did not wait.»
(جَيْبِكَ): the collar-opening of your shirt; it is called «جيب» because it is «يجاب», i.e., cut, so that the head may enter it.
(وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْها): istīqān is more intensive than īqān, so there is no sense in the saying of some exegetes that the sīn is merely additional.

* I'rab:
(إِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِأَهْلِهِ: إِنِّي آنَسْتُ ناراً): resumptive speech, brought to relate five of the stories of the ancients: the first is the story of Moses, followed by the story of the ants, then the story of Bilqīs, then the story of Ṣāliḥ, then the story of Lot. The adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; its determination has been given many times. The clause «قال» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «موسى» is the fāʿil (agent) and «لأهله» are attached to «قال». The clause «إني آنست نارا» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); «إن» and its noun, the clause «آنست» its khabar (predicate), and «نارا» the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «أهله» refers to his wife, the daughter of Shuʿayb, his child and his servant; that was on his return [Translator's note: the source prints «فقوله», evidently for «قفوله»] from Midian to Egypt to meet his mother and brother in Egypt. It has also been said that no one was with him but his wife, and Allah referred to her by «الأهل», and accordingly the address was given in the plural.
(سَآتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive. «آتيكم» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā" (I), and the kāf is the direct object. He used the sīn of deferment to indicate that he would return even if he were slow, for perhaps the distance was far. «منها» are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «خبر»; «بخبر» are attached to «آتيكم». «أو» is a conjunction; there is a secret in turning from the wāw to «أو», which will come in the Rhetoric section. «آتيكم» is conjoined to the first «آتيكم»; «بشهاب» are attached to «آتيكم»; «قبس» is a badal (substitute) of «شهاب», or a naʿt (adjective) of it on interpreting it as a passive, i.e., a flame taken from a fire. It was also read with annexation, because a shihāb may be a brand (qabas) or something else, like a star; so it is the annexation of the species to its genus, like «خاتم فضة» (a ring of silver) and «ثوب خز» (a garment of silk), and it carries the sense of «من». «لعلكم تصطلون»: the clause of hope is a ḥāl; «لعل», its noun and its khabar; i.e., hoping to secure and provide warmth for you.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَها نُودِيَ أَنْ بُورِكَ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَها): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted for brevity. «لما» is a temporal adverb meaning "when" (ḥīniyya), or a linking particle. «جاءها» is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. The clause «نودي» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «نودي» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he), referring to Moses. «أن» is the explicative (mufassira) one, because calling contains the meaning of saying without its letters, and the meaning is "it was said to him: blessed is…". It may also be in its normal function, i.e., making the imperfect verb accusative, here entering on a past verb; or lightened from the heavy (inna); and «أن» with what follows it is, as an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., «بأن بورك». There are other parsings which we have passed over because they are weak. «بورك» is a passive past verb, and «من» the deputy agent; «في النار» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «من», i.e., in the place of the fire. «ومن حولها» is conjoined to «من في النار». What is meant by «من» is either Allah the Exalted, with an omission, i.e., His power and authority; or, it has been said, Moses; or, it has been said, «من» refers to non-rational things, namely the light and the places around it.
(وَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; «سبحان» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; «الله» is muḍāf ilayhi; «رب العالمين» is a badal or an adjective.
(يا مُوسى إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): «يا» is a vocative particle and «موسى» is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper name. «إن» and its noun; the hāʾ is either the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) or refers to what the preceding indicates, i.e., "the one speaking to you". «أنا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الله» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إن»; «العزيز الحكيم» are two adjectives.
(وَأَلْقِ عَصاكَ فَلَمَّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّها جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِراً وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ألق» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you). The speech is conjoined to «بورك», because the meaning is "he was called: that blessed is the one in the fire, and that: throw your staff", and this is what makes it preferable that «أن» is explicative, as stated. «عصاك» is the object. «فلما»: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e., "so he threw it and it turned into a snake; and when…". «لما» is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking particle; the clause «رآها» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «رآها» is a verb, its agent and its direct object. The clause «تهتز» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, because the seeing here is visual. «كأنها جان»: «كأن», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl; or it is a ḥāl of the pronoun of «تهتز», making it an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. The clause «ولى» has no grammatical position, and «مدبرا» is a ḥāl of the agent of «ولى». The wāw is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive, and «يعقب» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم».
(يا مُوسى لا تَخَفْ إِنِّي لا يَخافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ): the clause is the object of an omitted saying which must be implied, i.e., the Exalted said. «يا موسى»: one addressed, a single proper name. «لا» is the prohibitive lā and «تخف» an imperfect verb, jussive by «لا». «إن» and its noun, and the clause «لا يخاف» its khabar; the clause gives the reason for the prohibition of fear. «لدي» is an adverb attached to «يخاف», and «المرسلون» is the agent.
(إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوءٍ): «إلا» is a particle of exception meaning "but" (lākin), because the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ); «من» is a relative noun, excepted, in the position of accusative. It may also be conditional, in which case it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause is excepted from the most general of states. «ظلم» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «ثم بدل» is conjoined to «ظلم»; «حسنا» is the direct object, and «بعد سوء» is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of «حسنا».
(فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ falls in the reply to «من» on both views; «إن», its noun and its two khabars.
(وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «أدخل» is conjoined to «وألق عصاك»; «يدك» is the direct object and «في جيبك» are attached to «أدخل». «تخرج» is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the reply to the command; the agent of «تخرج» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it). «بيضاء» is a ḥāl of the agent of «تخرج», and «من غير سوء» are attached to «بيضاء» because of the verbal meaning in it; this has preceded in Ṭāhā. Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that the preposition and its genitive noun be another ḥāl, and al-Samīn preferred that it be an adjective of «بيضاء».
(فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ): resumptive speech. The preposition is attached to the omitted verb, i.e., "go with nine signs to Pharaoh". Some determined it as an omitted word, i.e., "sent", so that its position is accusative as a ḥāl; the first is preferable, and it has parallels. The poet said:
فقلت إلى الطعام فقال منهم ... فريق يحسد الإنس الطعاما
(I said: "[Come] to the food!" and a party of them said: "We envy humans their food.")
There are many divergent views of the grammarians which we will give in the Benefits section to sharpen the mind.
«قومه» is conjoined to «فرعون». The clause «إنهم» gives the reason for the command to go; the clause «كانوا» is the khabar of «إن»; «قوما» is the khabar of «كانوا» and «فاسقين» an adjective. The nine signs have been discussed before.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ آياتُنا مُبْصِرَةً قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, as stated many times. «مبصرة» is a ḥāl, and its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position. «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «سحر» its khabar and «مبين» an adjective, and the clause is the object of the saying.
(وَجَحَدُوا بِها وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْها أَنْفُسُهُمْ ظُلْماً وَعُلُوًّا): «جحدوا» is conjoined to «قالوا»; «بها» are attached to «جحدوا». The wāw is of ḥāl, with «قد» implied after it. «استيقنتها أنفسهم» is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. «ظلما» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because it is the cause of the denial, or a ḥāl of the agent of «جحدوا», i.e., wrongdoing and arrogant.
(فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (of the implied condition). «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "anta". «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of «كان», and «عاقبة المفسدين» is the noun of «كان». The clause suspends «انظر» [Translator's note: the source prints «لا نظر», evidently for «لانظر»] from governing, so it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because «انظر» means "reflect".

* Rhetoric:
1- Using «أو» instead of the wāw:
In His words «آنست نارا سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون», He preferred «أو» to the wāw for a wonderful rhetorical point: «أو» conveys choice (takhyīr), and he built his hope on the idea that, if he did not obtain both his needs together, he would not lack one of them — either guidance on the road or taking a brand of fire — out of humility and acknowledgement of his shortcoming before his Lord. The night was wintry and dark, he had lost the road, and his wife had been seized by labour pains. This is a place where the pens of writers who do not grasp the secrets of eloquence slip, especially in the use of conjunctions and prepositions; this art has been pointed out before.
2- Majāz ʿaqlī (rational metaphor):
In attributing seeing to the signs in His words «فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة». It may also be a majāz mursal (synecdochic metaphor) whose relationship is causality, because they are the cause of seeing. This is better than the saying of some that «مبصرة» is an active participle by which the passive participle is meant — the active participle being applied to the passive to signal that, because of their extreme clarity and illumination, it is as if they would see themselves, were they among things that see.

* Benefits:
The views of the grammarians on «في تسع آيات»:
The views of the grammarians have diverged on the i'rab of this verse, «في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه». In the I'rab we have chosen for you the best and easiest of them, and we will give the remaining views, since they are reported and reasonable, so that they sharpen your mind and you may choose from them what you see as nearest to logic; for i'rab is logic before anything else.
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he confined himself to the view we chose in the I'rab. He said: «"في تسع آيات" is resumptive speech, and the preposition in it is attached to something omitted; the meaning is "go with nine signs", i.e., among the total of nine signs and their number. Someone may say: the signs were eleven, two of them the hand and the staff, and the nine are: the splitting [of the sea], the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the obliteration, drought in their deserts and decrease in their crops.»
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «في تسع» is a third ḥāl — by the first and second ḥāls he meant His word «بيضاء» and His words «من غير سوء» — and «إلى فرعون» is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "sent to Pharaoh"; it may also be an adjective of «تسع» or of «آيات», i.e., reaching Pharaoh.
Al-Zajjāj made «في» mean «من» and attached it to «ألق». He said: as you say «خد لي من الإبل عشرا فيها فحلان» [Translator's note: «خد» is as printed; «خذ» (take) is intended] — "take for me ten camels among which are two stallions", i.e., of them two stallions.
As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, he supported al-Zajjāj in attaching it to «ألق» and made «في» mean «مع» (with), because the hand and the staff are then included in the nine signs. He said: its implied sense is "that is prepared for you and spread among nine". Others said it is as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, but the hand and the staff are outside the nine.
Al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] chose that it be attached to an omitted word that is another ḥāl of the pronoun of «تخرج»; this omitted word is stated explicitly in Sūrat Ṭāhā, where He says: «تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى». So the meaning here is: being a sign included among the total of the nine signs.

dervis-irab:65-70.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ): this verse has occupied the exegetes, the parsers and the grammarians, and they have gone into it at length. We will choose here the easiest of their views, and will cite in the Benefits section everything that has been said about it, because of the enjoyable mental exercise in that. The clause is resumptive, introduced to answer them, since they had asked him about the time of the coming of the Hour. (لا) is negative and (يعلم) is an imperfect verb; (من) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم); (في السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من), i.e. "the one who is fixed, settled and dwelling in the heavens and the earth does not know"; (الغيب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إلا) is a particle of exception in the sense of "but" (lākin), indicating that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "knows". It is also correct for (من) to be in the position of the accusative as direct object, (الغيب) being a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of it and (الله) the agent of (يعلم), the meaning being: say, none knows the things that occur in the heavens and the earth, hidden from us, except Allah the Exalted. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (يشعرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أيان) is an interrogative noun meaning "when", accusative by (يبعثون), and it suspends (يشعرون) from governing, so the clause composed of it and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they are not aware of that. (بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْها بَلْ هُمْ مِنْها عَمُونَ): (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī). Al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] said it means (هل), which is strange, even though the commentators on al-Jalāl said that al-Jalāl's method is easier than the methods others followed. (ادارك) is a past verb, i.e. it caught up and followed in succession; al-Zamakhsharī cited twelve readings of it. (علمهم) is the agent; (في الآخرة) is attached to (ادارك) or to (علمهم). (ادارك), although past in form, is future in meaning, because it was certain, like His saying «أتى أمر الله». (بل) is also a particle of transitional digression; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (في شك) the khabar; (منها) is an adjective of (شك). (بل) is also a particle of transitional digression; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (منها) is attached to (عمون), and (عمون) is the khabar of (هم). The blindness here is blindness of the heart. The original form is ʿamiyūn: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was transferred to the mīm after its kasra was removed.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً وَآباؤُنا أَإِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ): the wāw is for conjunction; (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of (الذين). The hamza is for disapproving interrogation; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (كنا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (كان) and its noun, and (ترابا) is its khabar; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the noun of (كان), the conjunction to it being permitted by the separation with the khabar. The hamza is also for disapproving interrogation; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (مخرجون) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first clause. (لَقَدْ وُعِدْنا هذا نَحْنُ وَآباؤُنا مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): the clause is a second tawkīd of the preceding clause. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (وعدنا) is a passive past verb and (نا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (هذا) is the second object of (وعدنا); (نحن) is a tawkīd of (نا); (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the overt pronoun in (وعدنا), the conjunction being permitted by its emphasis with the detached pronoun and by the separation with the second object. (من قبل) is attached to (وعدنا), and the adverb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. before the coming of Muḥammad, by earlier messengers. Here an ellipsis required by concision must be supplied: "Had what we were promised been true, it would have happened." (إن) is negative; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أساطير) is the khabar of (هذا), and (الأولين) is muḍāf ilayhi.
(قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): (سيروا) is an imperative verb whose meaning is to threaten them for their denial and to warn them lest there befall them what befell the deniers before them; (في الأرض) is attached to (سيروا); (فانظروا) is conjoined to (سيروا); (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, the fronted khabar of (كان), and (عاقبة المجرمين) is the postponed noun of (كان). (وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا تَكُنْ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ): the wāw conjoins to (قل); (لا) is prohibitive; (تحزن) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (عليهم) is attached to (تحزن); (ولا تكن) is conjoined to (لا تحزن); the noun of (تكن) is latent, its implied form being "you"; (في ضيق) is the khabar; (مما) is an adjective of (ضيق), and the clause (يمكرون) is the ṣila.

* Benefits:
The origin of the confusion in this verse is that they — i.e. the grammarians — parsed the Glorious Name as a badal (substitute) of (من), and in that there is substituting the disconnected excepted, which is a less preferred usage of Tamīm; and since the reading in the nominative is among what the Seven agreed upon, that difficulty arose. In what we have mentioned — i.e. parsing the Glorious Name as a mubtadaʾ — there is an escape from all this. They said: «(الله) is nominative as a badal of (من), because He, the Exalted, is not contained by a place.»
Al-Ṣafāqusī permitted the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), the locative sense in His case, the Exalted, being figurative; in that there is a combination of the literal and the figurative in the locative sense. On this view it is nominative as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). We have previously set out the combining of the literal and the figurative in one word, and we preferred the permissibility of their combination; on that pattern is their saying «The pen is one of the two tongues». All the scholars of legal theory among the followers of Imam al-Shāfiʿī do not stipulate, for the figurative, the contextual indicator (qarīna) preventing the intention of the literal meaning.
Combining the literal and the figurative involves bringing the speech out contrary to what the apparent situation requires, and it is a kind of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ) called al-tanwīʿ (diversification): it is the claim that what a word names is of two kinds, conventional and non-conventional, by way of imagination. It is a wide kind that runs through many chapters. Among it is treating what occurs in the place of a thing, as a substitute for it, as having its status, without simile or metaphor, as in their saying «Their greeting among themselves is a painful blow» and their saying «His punishment is the sword».
Ibn al-Kamāl said: If you say, "How is Allah excepted, when He, the Exalted, is far above and exalted beyond being in the heavens and the earth?", I say: just as «غير أن سيوفهم» was excepted in his saying — that is, al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched from clashing with the battalions.)
That is: if Allah the Exalted were among those in the heavens and the earth, then there would be among them one who knows the unseen. The purpose is exaggeration in denying knowledge of the unseen to them and blocking the way to that possibility. So the exception is connected, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف», for the commentators on al-Kashshāf, all of them, stated explicitly that the exception in it is connected.
What is surprising is that al-Bayḍāwī permitted the exception to be connected in the verse on marriage in the manner mentioned, and here was decisive that it is disconnected. What appears from al-Zamakhsharī's words also is decisiveness about its being disconnected, since he said: «It is permissible to put the name of Allah the Exalted in the nominative according to the usage of Banū Tamīm, where they say "There is no one in the house except a donkey", as if "one" had not been mentioned.» For on supplying the speech according to the arrangement mentioned, putting the name of Allah in the nominative is also correct according to the usage of the people of the Ḥijāz.
Some objected to the second parsing — i.e. (من) in the accusative and (الغيب) parsed as a badal ishtimāl of (من) — saying that the badal ishtimāl requires a pronoun as a link, and there is no pronoun here; and the badal is not after the particle of exception, so that it could be said that the strength of the excepted's connection with what it is excepted from makes the pronoun unnecessary. On this basis the first view is free of every objection.

dervis-irab:71-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رَدِفَ): In al-Qāmūs: «radifahu, like samiʿa and naṣara: he followed him». But here it has been made to contain (ḍummina) the meaning of danā or qaruba ("drew near"), and for that reason it is made transitive with the lām; or the lām is redundant (zāʾida), as will come in the I'rab. It has also been made transitive with min; he said:
فلما ردفنا من عمير وصحبه ... تولوا سراعا والمنية تعنق
(When we came close upon ʿUmayr and his companions, they turned away in haste, while death sped after them.)
Radifa, like tabiʿa, is transitive by itself, and here it contains the meaning of al-dunuw (drawing near), so it is made transitive with min. Aʿnaqa al-faras: the horse went at a fast, easy pace, and al-ʿanaq is the noun from it. The poet says: when we drew near to ʿUmayr and his companions for battle, they turned their backs hastening, while death was hastening behind them from our side. He likened death to the lion by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) and attributed al-ʿanaq to it as an imaginative attribution (takhyīl), as if they had followed them by shooting arrows.
It may be that he borrowed "death" for himself and his people by way of explicit metaphor, i.e. "while we were hastening behind them"; then mentioning al-ʿanaq is a tajrīd (abstraction), because it suits the thing likened. Al-ʿanaq is a kind of pace of riding animals, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ.
Ibn al-Shajarī said:
The meaning of «ردف لكم» is "has followed you"; from it is the ridf of a woman (her buttocks), because it follows her from behind; and from it is the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
عاد السواد بياضا في مفارقه ... لا مرحبا ببياض الشيب إذ ردفا
(The black turned to white in the partings of his hair — no welcome to the whiteness of grey hair when it followed on!)
Al-Jawharī said: ardafahu is a dialectal variant of radifahu, like tabiʿahu and atbaʿahu, with the same meaning. Khuzayma ibn Mālik ibn Nahd said:
إذا الجوزاء أردفت الثريا ... ظننت بآل فاطمة الظنونا
(When Gemini followed the Pleiades, I had all manner of thoughts about the family of Fāṭima.)

* I'rab:
(وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the address is to the Prophet. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (متى) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (هذا) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الوعد) is a badal (substitute). (إن) is conditional and (كنتم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (كان) and its noun, and (صادقين) is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.
(قُلْ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُمْ بَعْضُ الَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): (عسى), (لعل) and (سوف), when used in addressing someone of greater standing than you, are tantamount to certainty about what they introduce; they use them only for dignity. (عسى) is a defective (jāmid) past verb, among the verbs of hope; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (أن يكون) is an interpreted maṣdar, its khabar. The noun of (يكون) is latent, its implied form being "it"; (ردف) is a past verb made to contain the sense of a verb transitive with the lām; (بعض) is the agent and (الذي) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (تستعجلون) is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause (ردف) is the khabar of (يكون). It is said that (ردف) keeps its proper sense, meaning "followed", and the lām is redundant. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (ذو فضل) is its khabar; (على الناس) is attached to (فضل) or is an adjective of it. The wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) that puts in the accusative; (أكثرهم) is its noun and the clause (لا يشكرون) is its khabar. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ ما تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām, and the clause (يعلم) is the khabar of (إن); (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (تكن صدورهم) is the ṣila, the referring pronoun being omitted; (وما يعلنون) is conjoined to (ما تكن). (وَما مِنْ غائِبَةٍ فِي السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (من) is a redundant preposition; (غائبة) is genitive in wording and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, beginning with an indefinite being permitted because negation enters upon it. Al-ghāʾiba is everything hidden: the thing that is absent and concealed is called ghāʾiba and khāfiya, the tāʾ in them having the same status as in al-ʿāfiya, al-ʿāqiba, al-naṣīḥa, al-ramiyya and al-dhabīḥa, in that they are nouns, not adjectives. It is permissible that these be adjectives with the tāʾ in them for intensiveness, like rāwiya, ʿallāma and nassāba. (في السماء والأرض) is an adjective of (غائبة); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (في كتاب) is the khabar of (غائبة), and (مبين) is an adjective. (إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَقُصُّ عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ أَكْثَرَ الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): the clause is resumptive, to explain another kind of the distinctions of the Qur'an. (إن) and its noun; (القرآن) is a badal of the demonstrative; the clause (يقص) is the khabar of (إن); (على بني إسرائيل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يقص); (أكثر) is the direct object and (الذي) is muḍāf ilayhi; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون), and the clause (يختلفون) is the ṣila of (الذي). [Translator's note: strictly the ṣila is the nominal clause (هم فيه يختلفون), with (يختلفون) as the khabar of (هم); the source states it as written.] (وَإِنَّهُ لَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): conjoined to what precedes; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām and (هدى) is its khabar; (رحمة) is conjoined to (هدى); (للمؤمنين) is an adjective. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ بِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْعَلِيمُ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يقضي) is its khabar; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (بحكمه) is attached to (يقضي); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) the first khabar and (العليم) the second khabar.

* Benefits:
Rules of the vowelled tāʾ attached to nouns and adjectives:
This tāʾ is one of the signs of the feminine specific to nouns, because, since the feminine is a branch of the masculine, it needed a sign to distinguish it. However, the Arabs have made many nouns feminine with an implied tāʾ, and that implied tāʾ is inferred from the pronoun referring to them, as in «النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا», «حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها» and «إن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها»; from pointing to them, as in «هذه جهنم»; and from its appearance in the diminutive of the noun, as in ʿuyayna and udhayna, diminutives of ʿayn (eye) and udhun (ear), among the paired limbs, for the diminutive returns things to their origins. The well-known rule is that among the limbs, what is paired is mostly feminine, except the two eyebrows, the two nostrils and the two cheeks, which are masculine; though the reference point is what is heard from the Arabs, for among the paired is the kaff (palm), which is feminine. Al-Mubarrad claimed that it may be masculine and recited:
ولو كفي اليمين تقيك خوفا ... لأفردت اليمين عن الشمال
(If my right hand were protecting you in fear, I would separate the right from the left.)
But this is a mistake by al-Mubarrad, for al-yamīn stands in the place of al-yumnā, so it is feminine.
Ibn Yasʿūn said: moreover, he returned to the feminine and said «تقيك». We return to the methods of inference and say: the implied tāʾ is also inferred from its appearance in its verb, as in «ولما فصلت العير», and from its absence from its numeral, as in the saying of Ḥumayd al-Arqaṭ describing an Arab bow:
أرمي عليها وهي فرع أجمع ... وهي ثلاث أذرع وأصبع
(I shoot with it while it is all of one top-branch, and it is three cubits and a finger.)
Adhruʿ is the plural of dhirāʿ, which is feminine, as shown by the absence of the tāʾ from its numeral, thalāth. The wāw in his words «وهي» is circumstantial [Translator's note: the source has «فرع للحال», evidently a slip for «للحال»]. One says qaws farʿ when it is made from the top of the branch. By his words «وأصبع» he did not mean literally the measure of a finger, but indicated by it the perfection of the bow, as you say "The cloth is seven cubits and more", meaning that it fully reaches this number.
Mostly this tāʾ serves to separate the feminine adjective from the masculine adjective, like qāʾima and qāʾim; less commonly it is found in nouns that are not adjectives, as in rajul and rajula, ghulām and ghulāma; and in adjectives that bear two intentions, namely adjectives specific to the feminine like ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith (menstruating): if what is intended is the occurrence at one of the times, the tāʾ is attached and one says ḥāʾiḍa and ṭāmitha; if that is not intended it is not attached, and one says ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith meaning "capable of menstruation".
In al-Mufaṣṣal he said: «The Basrans have two views regarding ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith: according to al-Khalīl it is relational (ʿalā al-nasab), like lābin and tāmir, as if it were said "one possessing menstruation"; and according to Sībawayh it is interpreted as "a menstruating person" or "thing", as in their saying ghulām rabʿa, interpreted as nafs. That is only in the permanent attribute; as for the occurring one, it must have the sign of the feminine, so you say "ḥāʾiḍa and ṭāliqa now or tomorrow".» We have explained the difference between the occurring and the permanent attribute in speaking of the saying of the Exalted «يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت»: the murḍiʿ is she whose role is to nurse, and the murḍiʿa is she who is in the state of nursing, putting her breast into the child's mouth; so look at it there.
In al-Mufaṣṣal he said: «The view of the Kufans is that dropping the tāʾ in ḥāʾiḍ is because there is no need for it.» This would require affirming the tāʾ where there is ambiguity, as in ḍāmir (lean), ʿāshiq (lover), ayyim (unmarried), thayyib (previously married) and ʿānis (spinster); and this objection is clear. As for the objection from affirming the tāʾ in adjectives specific to females, such as imraʾa muṣība and kalba mujriya, according to what is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, it is not sound, because what they mentioned is permissive, not obligatory, since they say that bringing the tāʾ where it is not needed returns to the original [Translator's note: the source's wording here is elliptical; translated by sense], as with ḥāmila for a woman. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "One says imraʾa ḥāmil and ḥāmila when she is pregnant. Whoever says ḥāmil says: this is an epithet only for females; and whoever says ḥāmila builds on ḥamalat fa-hiya ḥāmila." And he recited, by ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān:
تمخضت المنون له بيوم ... أتى ولكل حاملة تمام
(Fate went into labour for him with a day that came — and every pregnant one has her term.)
If she carries something on her back or on her head, then she is ḥāmila and nothing else.
Furthermore, this tāʾ does not enter five patterns:
1- faʿūl, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the sense of fāʿil, as in rajul jasūr and imraʾa jasūr; «وما كانت أمك بغيّا»; its mention has preceded in Sūrat Maryam.
2- faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as in rajul jarīḥ and imraʾa jarīḥ; if you say "I passed by the qatīla of Banū so-and-so", you attach the tāʾ for fear of confusion with the masculine, because you did not mention the qualified noun.
3- mifʿāl, with kasra on the mīm, as in minḥār; one says rajul minḥār and imraʾa minḥār.
4- mifʿīl, with kasra on the mīm, like miʿṭīr from ʿiṭr (perfume); imraʾa miskīna is irregular, and imraʾa miskīn has been heard according to the rule.
5- mifʿal, like mighsham, who is the one who does not desist from what he wants and desires, out of his courage.
The tāʾ of separation: the tāʾ comes to separate a single unit from the genus, like tamra and tamr, or to separate the genus from the single unit, as in kamʾa [Translator's note: the source has «كماة»]; and sayyāra in the saying of the Exalted «وجاءت سيارة» is not of this, for it is the plural of sayyār, not one of the generic nouns.
The tāʾ of compensation: it is the one that comes as compensation for a fāʾ, as in ʿida; or an ʿayn, as in iqāma; or a lām, as in sana; or for an extra letter not carrying meaning, as in zindīq and zanādiqa, where the tāʾ is compensation for the yāʾ of zanādīq.
The tāʾ of Arabicisation: it is the one that comes to Arabicise foreign nouns, as in mawāzija, plural of mawzaj — with fatḥa on the mīm, sukūn on the wāw, fatḥa on the zāy, followed by jīm — which is the khuff (leather sock) or the stocking; the regular form would be mawāzij, and the tāʾ entered its plural to indicate that its origin is foreign and it was Arabicised.
The tāʾ of intensiveness: the tāʾ of intensiveness in description, like rāwiya for one who transmits a great deal, and nassāba for one with great knowledge of genealogies.

dervis-irab:15-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَنْطِقَ الطَّيْرِ): «المنطق» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «نطق ينطق», of the pattern of ḍaraba: nuṭqan, manṭiqan and nuṭūqan, i.e., he spoke with sound and letters by which meanings are known. «المنطق» is speech, and it is sometimes used of other than humans: one says "I heard the manṭiq of the birds." Al-Bayḍāwī said: «Nuṭq and manṭiq in common usage are every utterance by which what is in the mind is expressed, whether single or compound, meaningful or not meaningful.
