Al-Bāqillānī takes up the sūra as a whole: he explains its rare words and shows its beauty of wording and meaning, and he begins analysing it from its start, saying: «He began with mentioning the sūra up to His making clear that the Qur'an is from Him; then He joined to that the story of Moses, and that he saw a fire and said to his family «امكثوا إني آنست نارا سآتيكم منها بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون», and He said in Sūrat Ṭā Hā in this story: «لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى». Then He said: «فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها وسبحان الله رب العالمين». Look at what He made the first speech run towards, how it connected with that introduction, and how He joined to it what follows of reports about Lordship, and what indicated it, of the transformation of eloquence [Translator's note: so in the source, «قلب الفصاحة»; presumably «قلب العصا», "the transformation of the staff", is meant], making it a proof guiding him to Him and a miracle leading him to Him. Look at the single words standing by themselves in beauty and in the noble meanings they contain; then at what He paired with this sign and joined to this proof, the white hand, from the light of the proof, without harm. Then look at verse after verse and word after word: do you find it as we described, of marvellous composition and novel description? Every word, were it taken alone, would be the utmost in beauty and a sign in indication; so how much more when its sisters are joined to it and its kind are combined with it, running in beauty its course and taking up its meaning; then from story to story and from chapter to chapter without any flaw occurring in the composition from section to section, until the section is depicted for you as a connection, by novel arrangement and eloquent revelation.»
Al-Bāqillānī shows the superiority of the composition of the Qur'an over ordinary speech: he invites one to imitate it, and he attains nothing and admits incapacity before the wording and composition of the Qur'an. He continues analysing the sūra, saying: «When could it be prepared for a human being to say, in describing the letter of Solomon, peace be upon him, after mentioning the address and the basmala, this lofty, noble word «ألّا تعلوا علي وأتوني مسلمين»; and to pass from that to what she arrived at of management and what she occupied herself with of consultation, and her magnifying the matter of the one consulted, and their magnifying her matter and obedience to her, with those novel words and marvellous expressions; then her speech after that — so that you know the firmness of her saying: «يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في أمري ما كنت قاطعة أمرا حتى تشهدون»; and He mentioned their saying: «قالوا نحن أولو قوة وأولوا بأس شديد والأمر إليك فانظري ماذا تأمرين» — you will not find in their description of themselves anything more novel than how He described them. His saying «الأمر إليك» — you know its excellence in itself, its marvellous meaning and the place of its precision in this speech, and the firmness of the verse-ending and its fitness for what precedes it, namely His saying: «فانظري ماذا تأمرين». Then [look] at this brevity, and at the clarity together with the inimitability; for speech may be spoiled by brevity and obscured by lightening and concision, but this is something that brevity only makes more expansive, because of its firmness and its falling in its proper place» — until he says: «If I were to explain to you what is in every verse, the matter would become long for you; but by what I have explained I have made clear, and by what I have detailed I have established, the way I have followed, the direction I intended, the aim at which I aimed and the path to which I have called.»
We reckon that after this you have become acquainted with the book on inimitability, for we have cited for you the best of what is in it.

dervis-irab:27-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَفْتُونِي): advise me. «الفتوى» is the answer concerning an incident; it was derived by way of metaphor from «الفتا» (youth) in age. What is meant by «الفتوى» here is their advising her with what they had, as we mentioned, concerning the opinion and plan that occurred to her. In al-Asās: «So-and-so is one of the people of fatwā and futyā; "come, let us go to judgment" (فتعالوا ففاتونا) [Translator's note: so in the source]; and «تفاتوا إليه»: they referred their dispute to him for judgment. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
هلمّ إلى قضاة الغوث فاسأل ... برهطك والبيان لدى القضاة
(Come to the judges of al-Ghawth and ask about your clan; clear proof lies with the judges.)
أنخ بفناء أشدق من عديّ ... ومن جرم وهم أهل التفاتي
(Make your camel kneel in the courtyard of an eloquent man of ʿAdī and of Jarm, for they are the people to whom disputes are referred.)
And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
فبتّ أفاتيها فلا هي ترعوي ... بجود ولا تبدي إباء فتبخلا
(I spent the night questioning her, and she neither relented with generosity nor showed refusal so as to be miserly.)
i.e., I asked her.»
The fāʾ may be given ḍamma or fatḥa [i.e., futwā and fatwā], as stated in Adab al-Kātib by Ibn Qutayba, who said: «They said: fatwā and futyā, baqwā and buqyā, thanwā and thunyā, raʿwā and ruʿyā.»
(أُولُوا قُوَّةٍ): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning "possessors"; its singular is «ذو» meaning "possessor". It has also been said that it is the plural of «ذو» not from its own wording. It has been stated before that it is among the words annexed to (treated like) the sound masculine plural. The feminine is «أولات», whose singular is «ذات»; you say: «جاء أولو العلم وأولات الفضل» (the men of knowledge and the women of merit came).

* I'rab:
(قالَ سَنَنْظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ): resumptive speech, brought to answer a question arising from the hoopoe's account. The clause «سننظر» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The hamza is interrogative; «صدقت» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «أم» is connective (muttaṣila), balancing the hamza; «كان» and its noun, and «من الكاذبين» its khabar (predicate). He turned from the verb corresponding to what preceded it to the noun for a rhetorical point indicated more than once before, namely making him one [Translator's note: the source prints «واحد» for «واحدا»] of the group branded with lying.
(اذْهَبْ بِكِتابِي هذا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَانْظُرْ ماذا يَرْجِعُونَ): some omitted speech must be implied so that the events of the story fit together, i.e.: then it showed them the water, and they drew it out, quenched their thirst, made ablution and prayed. Then Solomon wrote a letter, of this form: "From the servant of Allah Solomon to Bilqīs, queen of Sabaʾ. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission." Then he sealed it with his seal, then said to the hoopoe: "Go." So the clause is the object of an omitted saying. «اذهب» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you); «بكتابي» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اذهب»; «هذا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتابي» or a badal (substitute) of it. «فألقه»: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ألقه» is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إليهم» are attached to «ألقه» [Translator's note: the source prints «وأنهم متعلقان بألفه», evidently misprints for «وإليهم متعلقان بألقه»]. «ثم» is a conjunction; «تول» is an imperative verb [indeclinable] on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent, its implied form being "anta"; «عنهم» are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., passing beyond them to a nearby place where you can hide, so that what they say is within your hearing. «فانظر» is conjoined to «تول». «ماذا يرجعون»: in this expression there are two views:
The first: that «انظر» means "consider and reflect". Then «ماذا» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted object of «يرجعون», its implied sense being "what thing do they return"; or you make «ما» an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» a relative noun meaning "that which", the khabar of «ما», the clause «يرجعون» being the ṣila (relative clause) of «ذا», with the returning pronoun omitted, its implied sense being "what is the thing that they return?" On both determinations, the governing word, «انظر», has been suspended (muʿallaq) from the interrogative clause by the interrogative, so its position is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "look into such-and-such and reflect on it".
The second: that «انظر» means "wait", as in the words of the Exalted «انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم». Then «ماذا» as a whole is a relative noun — one of the uses of «ماذا» that will come in the Benefits section — and it is the direct object, i.e., "wait for what they return"; the clause «يرجعون» is the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, as stated. The meaning is: what answer they give back, or what words they exchange with one another.
(قالَتْ يا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ إِنِّي أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتابٌ كَرِيمٌ): some omitted speech must be implied, in whose omission concision was observed. Its implied form, as Muqātil said: «The hoopoe carried the letter in its beak and flew until it stopped over the woman's head, with the soldiers and armies around her. It fluttered for a while as the people watched; the woman raised her head, and it dropped the letter into her lap.» More reports concerning the determination of this omitted part will come.
«وإني»: «إن» and its noun; the clause «ألقي» is its khabar; «إليّ» are attached to «ألقي»; «كتاب» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and «كريم» an adjective. The secret of this description will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِنَّهُ مِنْ سُلَيْمانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to answer an implied question, as if they said: "From whom is it, and what does it contain?" So she said: it is from Solomon. «إن» and its noun, and «من سليمان» its khabar. «وإنه»: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun, and the clause of the basmala is its khabar. The i'rab of the basmala was given at the beginning of this book.
(أَلَّا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ وَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ): «أن» is explicative (mufassira), what it explains being «كتاب», because it includes the meaning of saying without its letters. «لا» is the prohibitive lā, «تعلوا» an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لا», the wāw is the agent, and «عليّ» are attached to «تعلوا». «أن» may also be maṣdariyya, making the verb accusative, with «لا» negative; «أن» with what falls in its scope is then an interpreted maṣdar, in the position of nominative as a badal of «كتاب», or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "its content is that you not exalt yourselves"; or in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., «بأن لا تعلوا». «وأتوني»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ائتوني» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the direct object. «مسلمين» is a ḥāl.
(قالَتْ يا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي أَمْرِي): «أفتوني» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is of protection and the yāʾ is the direct object; «في أمري» are attached to «أفتوني».
(ما كُنْتُ قاطِعَةً أَمْراً حَتَّى تَشْهَدُونِ): «ما» is negative; «كنت قاطعة»: «كان», its noun and its khabar; «أمرا» is the direct object. «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition; «تشهدون» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after «حتى», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the nūn present is the nūn of protection, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the direct object.
(قالُوا نَحْنُ أُولُوا قُوَّةٍ وَأُولُوا بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ): the clause «نحن» is the object of the saying; «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ and «أولو» its khabar, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is annexed to the sound masculine plural; «قوة» is muḍāf ilayhi; «وأولو بأس شديد» is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَانْظُرِي ماذا تَأْمُرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «الأمر» is a mubtadaʾ and «إليك» its khabar, i.e., it is entrusted to you and we obey you. «فانظري»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses something implied, as if they imagined that she might be desirous of fighting, or that they were desirous of it: "if you want that and are resolved to plunge into war, we are experts at it (abnāʾ bajdatihā)". «انظري» means "reflect". «ماذا» is an interrogative noun — its i'rab has preceded and its uses will come — and here it is in the position of accusative as a fronted object of «تأمرين»; the interrogative suspends the [verb of] considering.

* Rhetoric:
In this dialogue that took place between Bilqīs and the chiefs of her people, and in the description of Solomon's letter after mentioning the address and the basmala, there are numerous arts, the most important of which we give below:
1- Ishāra (allusion):
This art has been referred to earlier in this book. Qudāma derived it from the harmony of wording with meaning and explained it, saying: it is that a little wording indicates much meaning, so that the indication of the wording is like pointing with the hand, which by one movement points to many things. The difference between it and ījāz (concision) is that ījāz uses the words assigned to the meaning, while the words of ishāra are a quick, indicative glimpse; so the indication of wording in ījāz is indication by correspondence (dalālat muṭābaqa), while the indication of wording in ishāra is either indication by inclusion (taḍammun) or indication by entailment (iltizām); the indication here is by inclusion. She described Solomon's letter as noble (karīm) because it came from a noble king, or because it was sealed. In a ḥadīth it is reported from him ﷺ that he said: "The nobility of a letter is its seal." And from Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ: whoever writes a letter to his brother and does not seal it has made light of him.
It is related that she was asleep; when she slept, she would lock the doors and put the keys under her head. The hoopoe entered through a window-opening and dropped the letter on her throat while she lay on her back — it has also been said that it pecked her — and she woke up alarmed. When she saw the seal she trembled and said to her people what she said.
2- Ījāz (concision):
In their words «قالوا نحن أولو قوة وأولو بأس شديد والأمر إليك فانظري ماذا تأمرين» there is a wonderful concision. First, it indicates the magnifying of consultation and Bilqīs's magnifying the standing of the one consulted; second, it indicates their magnifying her command and obeying her. In their words «والأمر إليك» and «فانظري ماذا تأمرين» there is a concision that intoxicates minds. Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Ṭayyib al-Bāqillānī said in his book Iʿjāz al-Qur'an: «Speech may be spoiled by abridgement and obscured by lightening and concision; but this is among what abridgement only expands, because of its firmness and its falling in its proper place, and its concision contains a versatility that goes beyond its place and position» — until he says: «You will find in all that we have recited to you only what, when expanded, gives benefit, and when abridged is complete and excellent in its kind; and when the wise man lets the glance of his thought roam over its sides, and the learned man sends the eyes of his inquiries into its edges, they fall only upon beauties following one another and marvels coming in succession.»

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām devoted a section of al-Mughnī to «ماذا», which we summarize below, parsing its examples:
«ماذا» comes in Arabic in several ways:
1- That «ما» is interrogative and «ذا» a demonstrative, as in «ماذا التواني؟» (what is this slackness?) and «ماذا الوقوف؟» (what is this standing still?). «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» its khabar; «التواني» is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), i.e., "what thing is this slackness?"
2- That «ما» is interrogative and «ذا» a relative, as in the words of Labīd:
ألا تسألان المرء ماذا يحاول ... أنحب فيقضي أم ضلال وباطل
(Will you two not ask a man what it is he strives for: a vow he fulfils, or error and vanity?)
«ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; «ذا» is a relative noun, its khabar; the clause «يحاول» is the ṣila; the hamza is interrogative, and «نحب» is a badal of «ما».
3- That «ماذا» as a whole is an interrogative, by compounding, as when you say «لماذا جئت؟» (why did you come?), and the poet's words:
يا خزر تغلب ماذا بال نسوتكم ... لا يستفقن إلى الديرين تحنانا
(O squint-eyed ones of Taghlib, what is the matter with your women, that they never recover from longing for the two monasteries?)
«ماذا» is a compound interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «بال نسوتكم» its khabar.
4- That «ماذا» as a whole is a generic noun meaning "a thing", or a relative meaning "that which", according to a disagreement over the interpretation of the poet's words:
دعي ماذا علمت سأتقيه ... ولكن بالمغيّب نبئيني
(Leave aside what you know — I shall guard against it — but tell me of what is hidden.)
The majority hold that «ماذا» as a whole is the object of «دعي»; then they differed: it has been said that it is a relative meaning "that which", and it has been said that it is an indefinite noun meaning "a thing". There are two other ways which Ibn Hishām mentioned, but we saw no need for them because they do not occur in eloquent speech.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: ﴿وكتابٍ مُبين﴾ is genitive; He means: and the verses of a clear Book. Had it been read ﴿وكتابٌ مبينٌ﴾, by referring it back to "the verses" [i.e. in the nominative], He would mean: and that is a clear Book. And if it were accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ) — as one says: "I passed by a handsome man, and a tall, strapping one (wa-ṭawīlan sharmaḥan)" — that is a valid way. Praise is like his saying:
إلى الملِك القَرْم وابنِ الهُمَام * وليْثَ الكَتيِبة فى المزدَحَمْ
(To the king, the chief, son of the valiant lord — and the lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)
In praise, both its definite and its indefinite are put in the accusative.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿هُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ﴾ is nominative, and if you wish you may put it in the accusative. The accusative is by severance (ʿalā al-qaṭʿ, i.e. as a ḥāl), and the nominative is by a new beginning (istiʾnāf). Similar to it in al-Baqara: ﴿هُدًى للمتَّقِين﴾; and in Luqmān: ﴿هُدىً ورَحْمَةً لِلمُحْسِنِين﴾ is like it.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash put tanwīn on al-shihāb and al-qabas, and the people of Medina made it a genitive construct: (بشهابِ قَبَسٍ). This is like His saying ﴿وَلَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ﴾: of the kind in which a thing is annexed to its own name when its names differ.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾: You make (أَنْ) in the position of the accusative if you take the name of Mūsā as latent in ﴿نُودى﴾; and if you do not take the name of Mūsā as latent, (أن) is in the position of the nominative: "that was called out". In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy: (أَنْ بُورِكتِ النارُ) ("that the fire has been blessed"). ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ means the angels. The Arabs say: bārakaka Allāh, bāraka fīka and bāraka ʿalayka (may Allah bless you).

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾: this hāʾ is the hāʾ of ʿimād (the support pronoun, i.e. the pronoun of the matter). It is a noun that does not appear [as a referent]. It has already been explained.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ﴾: al-jānn is the snake that is neither large nor small. His saying: ﴿وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِراً وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾: he did not turn round.
His saying: ﴿إِنِّي لاَ يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾; then He made an exception, saying: ﴿إَلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوۤءٍ﴾ — so this one is forgiven. Someone may say: how was he made one who fears? I say: there are two views on this. One is that you say: the messengers are protected (maʿṣūma), forgiven and safe on the Day of Resurrection, while whoever has mixed a righteous deed with another evil one fears and hopes; that is one view. The other is that you make the exception from those left out of the statement, because the meaning is: the messengers do not fear; fear is only for others than them.
Then He made the exception, saying: except whoever did wrong — for this one does not fear. He means: he was an idolater, then repented and did good, so that one is forgiven, not fearful.
Some grammarians have said that (إلا) in the language is equivalent to wāw (and), and that the meaning of this verse is: the messengers do not fear in My presence, nor does whoever did wrong and then substituted good. They made similar to it the saying of Allah: ﴿لِئَلاّ يَكُونَ لِلناسِ عَلَيْكمْ حُجَّةٌ إلاّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾, i.e. "nor those who did wrong". I have not found that Arabic tolerates what they said, because I do not allow "The people stood except ʿAbd Allāh" while he is standing; exception is only that the noun after illā is taken out of the meaning of the nouns before illā. I do consider it permissible to say "You owe a thousand besides (siwā) another thousand"; if you put (إلاّ) in this position it is sound, and (إلاّ) then has the interpretation they gave. But [illā] on its own [135/b], where a small part is excepted from a large whole — no. Rather, what is like it is that which comes in the meaning of illā, like the meaning of the wāw, without being it [Translator's note: the source has «الولو», evidently for «الواو»].
His saying: ﴿خَالِدِين فِيهَا ما دَامَتِ السَّموَاتُ والأرْضُ إلاّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾: in meaning it is "except (i.e. besides) what your Lord wills of increase". So do not make illā equivalent to the wāw, but equivalent to siwā (besides). When siwā is in the position of illā, it is sound in the meaning of the wāw, because you say "I have much wealth besides this", i.e. and this too I have — as though you said: I have much wealth, and this. It is more effective with siwā than with illā, because you may say "I have besides this (siwā hādhā)", but you do not say "illā hādhā".

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿واضْمُم يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ﴾: its meaning is: do this, and it is a sign among nine. Then He said ﴿إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ and did not say "sent" or "dispatched", because his affair is known: that he was sent to Pharaoh. The poet said:
رأتنى بحبليها فصَدَّت مخافةً * وفى الحبل رَوْعاء الفؤاد فَرُوق
(She saw me with her two ropes and shied away in fear; and on the rope was a skittish-hearted, timid one.)
He meant: she saw me coming with her two ropes — with the two ropes of the she-camel — so he left a verb implied, as though he said: she saw me approaching.
His saying ﴿وَإلَى ثَمودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالحاً﴾: accusative by an implied ﴿أرسلنا﴾ (We sent).

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَحَدُواْ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْماً وَعُلُوّاً﴾: he says: they denied the nine signs after their souls had become certain that they were from Allah, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ظلماً عُليّاً), like His saying ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكِبَر عُتيّاً﴾ and ﴿عِتِيّا﴾.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ﴾: Dāwūd had — according to what they mention — nineteen male children; Sulaymān was singled out for the inheritance only because it was the inheritance of kingship.
His saying ﴿عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾: the meaning of the speech of the birds; He made it like a man's speech since it was understood. The poet said:
عجبت لَهَا أنَّى يكُون غِناؤها * رَفيعاً ولم تَفتح بمنطقهَا فما
(I marvelled at her: how could her singing be so lofty, when she did not open a mouth for her speech?)
The poet made it like speech since he took it that she was weeping.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَحُشِرَ لِسْلَيْمَانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْس وَٱلطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾: these kinds used to be with Sulaymān when he rode out. ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾: the first of them were held back for the last of them until they gathered together. It is from wazaʿtu al-rajul (I restrained the man); you say: "I shall surely restrain you (la-azaʿannakum) from wrongdoing", and this is from that.

farraa:19-19.t: As for His saying: ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ﴾, its meaning is: inspire me.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾: the people read it with ḍamma [makutha], and ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa: fa-makatha. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (فتمكَّث). The meaning of ﴿غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾ is: not long in staying; "distant" and "long" are close [in meaning].
His saying ﴿فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ وَجِئْتُكَ﴾: some of the Arabs said aḥaṭṭu, putting the ṭāʾ in place of the tāʾ. When ṭāʾ meets tāʾ and the ṭāʾ before it is vowelless, the Arabs turn the ṭāʾ into tāʾ and say aḥattu, just as they turn the ẓāʾ into tāʾ in His saying ﴿أَوَعَتَّ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الواعِظِينَ﴾, and the dhāl and the dāl into tāʾ, as in ﴿أَخَتُّمْ﴾ — I saw it in some of the copies of ʿAbd Allāh as (وأَخَتُّمْ). And some of the Arabs turn the tāʾ, when it comes after the ṭāʾ, into ṭāʾ and say: aḥaṭṭ.
His saying ﴿وجئْتُكَ مِنْ سبَأ بِنَبإٍ يَقِينٍ﴾: the readers treat ﴿سَبأ﴾ as fully declinable (ijrāʾ), because — according to what they mention — it is a man; likewise make it declinable if it is the name of a mountain. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ did not make it declinable. Al-Ruʾāsī claimed he asked Abū ʿAmr about it and he said: I do not know what it is. He took a [reasonable] position, since he did not know what it was, because when the Arabs name [something] with an unknown name they leave it undeclined, as al-Aʿshā said:
وتدفنُ منه الصَّالحاتُ وإن يُسئْ * يكن ما أساء النارَ فى رأس كَبْكَبا
(His good deeds are buried, while if he does ill, his ill becomes a fire on the top of Kabkab.)
[136/a] It is as though he did not know Kabkab. I heard Abū al-Saffāḥ al-Salūlī say: "This is Abū Ṣuʿrūr, he has come," and he did not decline it, because it is not in their custom of naming.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-ṣuʿrūr is something like gum.
The poet said, not declining it:
الواردون وتيم فى ذُرَا سَبَأٍ * قد عضّ أعْنَاقَهم جلدُ الجواميسِ
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the heights of Sabaʾ — the hide of buffaloes has bitten into their necks.)
[Translator's note: in the verse as given here سَبَأٍ carries tanwīn, though it is cited for non-declension.] And if you made it the name of the tribe, if it is a man, or the name of what is around it, if it is a mountain, you would not make it declinable either.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ للَّهِ﴾: It is read ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ﴾, with ﴿يَسجْدوا﴾ in the position of the accusative; so Ḥamza read it. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan and Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it without doubling: (ألاَ يَسْجُدُوا), in the sense of "Lo! O you, prostrate!": "you" (hāʾulāʾ) is implied, and (يا) alone suffices for it. He said: I heard some of the Arabs say: "alā yā irḥamānā, alā yā taṣaddaqā ʿalaynā" (Lo! O, have mercy on us both; Lo! O, give alms to us both). He said: he meant me and my companion. The poet — al-Akhṭal — said:
أَلاَ يا اسلمى يا هند هندَ بنى بَدْر * وإن كان حَيَّاناَ عِدىً آخِر الدهر
(Lo! O be safe, O Hind, Hind of Banū Badr, even if our two clans are enemies to the end of time.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: one of the shaykhs — namely al-Kisāʾī — related to me from ʿĪsā al-Hamdānī, who said: I never heard the shaykhs read it except without doubling, intending the imperative. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (هَلاّ تسجدونَ لله) with tāʾ, and this is evidence for whoever reads it without doubling. In the reading of Ubayy: (أَلاَ تسجدونَ لله الذى يعلم سِرَّكم ومَا تَعلِنُون), and that is the proper sense of the passage, because it is a prostration [verse]. Whoever reads ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُوا﴾ with doubling, it ought not to be a prostration [verse], because the meaning is: Satan made it fair-seeming to them that they should not prostrate; and Allah knows best about that.
His saying ﴿يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ﴾ is with hamza. It is the unseen: the unseen of the heavens and the unseen of the earth. It is also said: it is the water that comes down from the sky and the vegetation from the earth. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (يخرج الخَبْءَ منَ السَّواتِ) [Translator's note: so in the source, for السموات]. (فى) is sound in place of (من) because you say "I shall surely extract from you the knowledge that is in you", and then you omit whichever of the two you wish — I mean (من) and (فى) — and the meaning remains as it is.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ﴾: Someone may say: how did he order it to turn away from them, when he said ﴿فانْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾? That is clear in Arabic: he urged it on, saying: "Go with this letter of mine and hurry"; then ﴿فانظر ماذا يَرجعونَ﴾ was placed later, while its meaning is placed earlier. It is also said that he ordered the hoopoe to drop the letter and then hide from her, and it did so: it dropped the letter and flew to an opening in the wall of her council chamber. Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتَابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: she called it noble because it was sealed; so I was told. It is also said: she described the letter as noble to her people because she saw the letter of a king with her, so she called it noble for the nobility of its sender. It is also said that she said (كريم) before she knew that it was from Sulaymān. That does not please me, because she was literate and had read the letter before going out to her council.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾: both are with kasra, I mean inna and inna. Had both been with fatḥa it would be permissible, according to your saying: "it was cast to me that it is from Sulaymān and that it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Their position is then nominative, by repetition (takrīr, i.e. substitution) for "the letter": "it was cast to me that it is from Sulaymān". And if you wish, they are in the position of the accusative because of the dropping of the preposition from them. In the reading of Ubayy: (وأَنْ بِسمِ الله الرحمن الرحيم), and that is evidence for whoever reads both with fatḥa, because (أَن), when its alif is with fatḥa with a verb or with what is quoted, can only be with the nūn lightened.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَعْلُواْ﴾: its alif is with fatḥa; kasra is not permissible. It is in the position of the nominative if you make it a repetition on ﴿أُلْقِى﴾, and accusative on [the sense]: "the letter was cast to me with this (bi-dhā)", and then you dropped the bāʾ and put it in the accusative. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وإنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم), and this indicates the kasra, because it is conjoined to: "Indeed, it was cast to me", "and indeed it is from Sulaymān". In the reading of Ubayy, it may be that you make the (أَن) that is in "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate" the same (أن) as in His saying ﴿أن لا تعلوا عَلىَّ﴾, as though in meaning: "it was cast to me: that you not exalt yourselves against me". When it was placed in (بسمِ الله), it was repeated in its position in ﴿أن لا تعلوا﴾, just as Allah said: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنّكُمْ إذا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ﴾ — "annakum" is repeated and its meaning is one, and Allah knows best. Do you not see that the meaning is: does he promise you that you will be brought out when you have become dust and bones?

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلأُ أَفْتُونِي﴾: she made consultation a fatwā (legal opinion). That is permissible because of the breadth of Arabic.
His saying ﴿مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْراً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ما كنتُ قاضيةً أمراً), and the meaning is the same. You say: I do not decide (lā aqṭaʿu) a matter without you, and I do not settle (lā aqḍī) a matter without you.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُواْ قَرْيَةً﴾ is an answer to their saying ﴿نَحْنُ أُولُو قُوَّةٍ وأولُو بأسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾. She said: if they enter your land they will humiliate you, though you are kings. And Allah said: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾: the alif is dropped from His saying (بم) because it means "with what thing will the envoys return?" When (مَا) is in the position of (أىّ, which?) and is then joined to a preposition that governs the genitive, the alif of (مَا) is dropped so that the interrogative is distinguished from the statement. Of this kind is His saying ﴿فِيمَ كُنْتم﴾ and ﴿عَمَّ يتساءَلُونَ﴾; and if you write it in full, that is correct. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سَرَاتكم * أهلَ اللوَاء ففيما يكثر القِيلُ
(We have killed your chiefs, the bearers of the banner, for our slain; so over what is there so much talk?)
And al-Mufaḍḍal also recited to me:
على ما قام يشتمنَا لَئِيمٌ * كخنزير تمرَّغ فى رمَادِ
(Over what does a base man stand up to revile us, like a pig rolling in ashes?)
His saying: ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ﴾ — she means Sulaymān — is like His saying ﴿عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهمْ﴾. And she said ﴿بِمَ يَرْجِعُ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾, while her envoy — according to what they mention — was a single woman; she used the plural while it was only one envoy. That is why He said ﴿فلمَّا جَاءَ سُلَيْمانَ﴾, meaning: when the envoy came to Sulaymān. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فلما جَاءوا سليمان); since He said ﴿المرسَلونَ﴾, ﴿جَاءوا﴾ is sound [too], though the one sent was one. This is indicated by Sulaymān's saying ﴿ارْجِعْ إليْهِمْ﴾.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is with two nūns and a written yāʾ. Ḥamza read it (أَتُمِدُّونَّى بمالٍ): he means the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, but he assimilated the nūn into the nūn and doubled it. ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read (أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بمالٍ) with two nūns without yāʾ. All are correct.
His saying: ﴿فَمَآ آتَانِيَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — and he did not say ﴿فما آتانِىَ الله﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the contrast intended is evidently between the yāʾ-less written form آتانِ and the form with the yāʾ] — because it is written without the yāʾ in the text (al-kitāb). Whoever is among those who allow adding to the Qurʾān the yāʾs and wāws that are dropped — as in His saying ﴿وَيَدْعُ الإنْسَان بالشَّرِّ﴾, where he writes in the wāw though it is not in the muṣḥaf, or [reads] al-munādī for al-munād — may say ﴿أتمدُّونَنِ﴾ with the yāʾ, and may vowel it [137/a] with the accusative fatḥa, as was said ﴿وَمَالِىَ لاَ أَعْبُدُ﴾; likewise ﴿فَمَا آتانِىَ الله﴾ is permissible. But I do not care for that, nor do I adopt it. Following the muṣḥaf, when I find a way for it in the speech of the Arabs and the reading of the readers, is dearer to me than departing from it. Abū ʿAmr used to read (إنَّ هَذَيْنِ لسَاحِرَان), and I do not dare to do that; and he read ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُونَ﴾, adding a wāw to the text, and I do not favour that.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ قِبَلَ لَهُمْ بِهَا﴾: in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh it is (لَهُمْ بهم), and it is the same.
His saying: ﴿ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾: this is from Sulaymān's words to her envoy — he means [the envoy of] Bilqīs. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ارجعوا إليهم), and that is correct, according to what I explained to you about His saying ﴿يأيُّها النَّبىّ إذا طلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾: addressing one person while meaning those with him, which occurs in much speech.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿عِفْرِيتٌ مِّن ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ﴾: al-ʿifrīt is the strong and effective one. Some of the Arabs say ʿifriya for ʿifrīt. Whoever says ʿifriya says in its plural ʿafārin; and whoever says ʿifrīt says ʿafārīt, and he may also say ʿafārin. In one of the two readings: (وَما أُهِلَّ بِهِ للطواغِى), meaning the plural of ṭāghūt. His saying ﴿أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقُومَ مِنْ مَقَامِكَ﴾ means: before he rises from the seat of judgement; he used to sit until midday. He said: I want [something] quicker (than that).

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ ٱلَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾: he says: before the thing reaches you from the extent of your sight. Ibn ʿAbbās said about His saying (عِنْدهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الكتاب): ﴿يا حَىُّ يا قيُّوم﴾ ("O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting"). It is mentioned that her throne sank into the ground in its place and then sprang up at Sulaymān's seat.

farraa:41-41.t: As for His saying: ﴿نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا﴾: he ordered them to enlarge it, in order to test her intelligence when she came. The devils had feared that Sulaymān would marry her, so they said: there is something [wrong] in her mind, and her leg is like the leg of a donkey. So Sulaymān ordered the throne to be changed for that reason, and ordered water, which was made to run beneath the glass pavilion (al-ṣarḥ), with fish in it. When she came, it was said to her: (أَهَكَذَا عَرْشُكِ). She recognised it and did not recognise it; she did not say "It is it", nor "It is not it", but said (كَأنَّه هُوَ). Then she lifted her garment from her shins, thinking she was walking into a lujja — a lujja is a great body of water — and he looked upon the most beautiful shins and feet. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وَكَشَفَ عَنْ رِجْليهَا) ("and she uncovered her feet").

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ﴾: he says: she was intelligent; what kept her from the worship of Allah was only the worship of the sun and the moon, which was a custom of her forefathers' religion. The meaning of the passage: what she used to worship — i.e. her worship of the sun and moon — kept her from worshipping Allah. (ما) is in the position of the nominative. It has also been said: ﴿إن صدَّها﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; read: «صدَّها»]: Sulaymān prevented her from what she used to worship; [then] the position of (ما) is accusative, because the verb belongs to Sulaymān. Some of them said: the verb belongs to Allah the Exalted: Allah kept her from what she used to worship.
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾: the alif has kasra, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). And if a reader read ﴿أنَّها﴾, he would refer it back to the position of (ما) in its nominative: "that she was of a disbelieving people kept her from the worship of Allah". It is like your saying: "What I was engaged in kept me from visiting you — that I was going out early and coming back late": anna explains the meaning of "what I was engaged in".

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾: the meaning of ﴿يختصمُونَ﴾ is: differing — a believer and a denier.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ طَائِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: he says: in the Preserved Tablet with Allah. You take me as an ill omen and augur ill of me, and all of that is from Allah. It is like His saying ﴿قالوا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ﴾, i.e. it is bound to you: whatever there is of good or evil is bound upon your necks. He has made it clear in His saying ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ ألْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فىعُنُقِهِ﴾.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ تَقَاسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (تقاسَمُوا بالله), without ﴿قالوا﴾. His saying: ﴿لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ﴾: tāʾ, nūn and yāʾ have all been read. Whoever says ﴿تقاسموا﴾ and makes ﴿تقاسموا﴾ a statement (khabar, i.e. a past verb), it is as though he said "swearing to one another": ﴿لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ﴾ with the nūn. Then the yāʾ is permissible with this meaning, so you say: they said ﴿ليبيتُنَّه﴾ with yāʾ, just as you say lanaqūmanna, layaqūmanna and layaqūmunna. Whoever says taqāsamū and makes it in the position of the jussive [i.e. an imperative], it is as though he said: "Make a pact and swear: you shall surely attack him by night (latubayyitunnahu)" with tāʾ. And the nūn is permissible in this respect, because the one who said to them "swear to one another" is included with them in the act, even though he commanded them; do you not see that you say "Stand up, let us go (nadhhab) to so-and-so", because he commands them while being with them in the act? The nūn is the most pleasing of the options to me. Al-Kisāʾī reads with tāʾ, and the generality [of readers] are on the nūn. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (تقاسَمُوا) (ثم لنُقْسِمَنًّ ما شهِدْنَا مَهْلك أهله). Allah has said ﴿تَعَالَوا نَدْعُ أَبْنَاءَنا وأبْنَاءَكُمْ﴾, because they called them so that all of them should do together what they called them to. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read it with the nūn, and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh with the tāʾ. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related to me from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj from Mujāhid that he read (ليُبَيِّتُنَّه) with the yāʾ.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾: It is read with kasra, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), like His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنسانُ إلَى طَعَامِهِ أنّا صَبَبْنَا الماءَ﴾: he begins anew while explaining by it what came before. And whoever refers it back to what came before [Translator's note: the source has «على إعلى», a scribal slip for «على»] says (أَنَّا) with fatḥa; then (أَنَّا) is in the position of the nominative, made to follow "the outcome" (al-ʿāqiba). And if you wish, you may make it accusative in two ways: one is to refer it to the position of (كيف); the other is to repeat (كان), as though you said: "the outcome of their plotting was Our destroying them". And if you wish, you may make it a single phrase and put (أَنَّا) in the position of the accusative, as though you said: "so look how the outcome of their plotting was: Our destroying them". And His saying: ﴿وأنتم تبصرونَ تعلمون أَن فاحشة﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a fragment concerning 27:54].

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾: It was said to Lūṭ: ﴿قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ for the destruction of those who were destroyed, ﴿وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾. ﴿ءَآللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: he says: is the worship of Allah better, or the worship of idols?

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ﴾: He said ﴿ذاتَ﴾ and did not say dhawāt, and each is correct. It is permissible to say ﴿ذات﴾ for "gardens", which is a plural, only because you say "these are gardens" just as you say "this is a garden". Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿وَلِلّهِ الأسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾, where He did not say al-ḥusan, and (والقُرون الأولَي). Had it been "gardens dhawāt bahja", it would be correct. Al-Aʿshā said, using the singular form:
فسوف يُعقبُنيهِ إن ظفرتَ به * ربٌّ غفورٌ وبِيض ذات أطهار
(A forgiving Lord will requite me for it, if you get hold of it, and fair women of purity.)
He did not say dhawāt aṭhār. Ḥadīqa is said only of every orchard that has a wall around it; what has no wall around it is not called ḥadīqa.
His saying: ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ refers back to His saying ﴿أَمْ مَنْ خَلَق﴾ such-and-such. Then He said ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ created it? And if you wish, you may make its nominative due to maʿa, as in your saying: "Is there with Allah — woe to you! — a god?" And it could come in the accusative, aʾilāhan maʿa Allāh, by implying a verb through which the accusative arises, as in your saying: "Do you set up a god with Allah?" or "Do you take a god with Allah?"
The Arabs say: "A fox, and you run away?!" (a-thaʿlaban wa-tafirru), as though they meant: "Do you see a fox and run away?" One of the poets said:
أَعبداً حلَّ فى شُعَبىَ غريباً * أَلُؤْماً لا أبالكَ واغترابَا
(A slave settling as a stranger in Shuʿabā? Baseness — may you have no father! — and being a stranger too?)
He means: do you combine baseness and estrangement? I heard one of the Arabs [speak] of a captive he had taken by night; when [138/a] morning came he saw that he was black, and said: "A slave, the whole night through!", as though he said: do I not see that I have captured a slave since my night [began]? Another said:
أجَخْفا تميميّاً إذا فتنة خَبَتْ * وجُبْناً إذا ما المشرفيّة سُلَّت
(Boastfulness, O Tamīmī, when strife has died down, and cowardice when the Mashrafī swords are drawn?)
This is in every [expression of] wonder in which they address the person concerned. But when one wonders at something while addressing someone else, they make the verb govern and say: "A fox, and a man running away from it!" [a-thaʿlabun wa-rajulun yafirru minhu], because this is addressed to someone other than the one with the fox. And if it were put in the accusative according to "Does a man run away from a fox?", you would make the conjoined as though it were the preceding element; it is built on this. I heard one of Banū ʿUqayl recite, by Majnūn of Banū ʿĀmir:
أألبرقَ أم نارا لليلى بدت لنَا * بمُنْخَرقٍ من سَارياتِ الجنائبِ
(Was it lightning, or a fire of Laylā, that appeared to us in a wind-swept tract of the night-travelling south winds?)
And he recited to me in it:
بل البرقَ يبدو فى ذَرَى دَفَئيَّة * يضىء نَشَاصاً مشمخرّ الغَوارب
(Nay, it was lightning appearing in the peaks of a spring cloud, lighting up towering cloud-masses with lofty crests.)
He put all of this in the accusative, with its verb accompanying it, by implying a verb of it, as though he said: do I see a fire? Nay, I see lightning. And as though he said: and if I [only] saw the fire of Laylā. Likewise the other two verses, in His saying ﴿أَإِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاواتِ وٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾: You put what comes after (إلاّ) in the nominative because in what precedes it there is a negation (jaḥd), and it [the preceding noun] is nominative. Had it been accusative it would be correct. In one of the two readings: ﴿مَا فعَلوهُ إلا قليلاً منهم﴾ in the accusative, and in our reading in the nominative; each is correct. This is when the negation before illā is with definite nouns. When it is with an indefinite, they say nothing but the following [construction] (itbāʿ) of what precedes (إلاّ); they say: "No one went except your father (abūka)", and they do not say "except abāka". That is because "the father" takes the place of "anyone": this is one and that is one, so they preferred itbāʿ. In the first case, what precedes (إلاَّ) is a plural and what follows (إلاّ) is one of it or part of it, not all of it.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلِ ٱدَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: its meaning is: perhaps their knowledge has come in succession (tadāraka). He says: their knowledge of the Hereafter followed in succession; he means: with knowledge of the Hereafter, whether it will be or not. That is why He said ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهَا بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: (أَمْ تداركَ عِلمُهُم فى الآخرة) with am. The Arabs put (بل) in place of (أم) and (أم) in place of (بل) when there is an interrogative at the beginning of the speech, as in the poet's saying:
فواالله ما أجرِى أسَلْمَى تَغَوَّلتْ * أم النومُ أم كلّ إلى حَبِيبُ
(By Allah, I do not know: has Salmā changed like a ghoul, or is it sleep, or are all dear to me?)
Their meaning is: bal (nay rather). The readers differed over ﴿ادّارك﴾: Yaḥyā, al-Ḥasan, Shayba and Nāfiʿ read (بل ادَّاركَ); and Mujāhid [and] Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read (بَلْ أَدْرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِى الآخِرة), from adraktu (I attained), and its meaning is as though he said: has their knowledge attained the knowledge of the Hereafter? It has reached me from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (بَلَى أَدَّارك), as a question, doubling the dāl and putting a yāʾ in (بلى). That is a good reading, because it is more like mockery of the deniers, as in your saying to a man you are calling a liar: "Yes indeed (balā), by my life, you have met the predecessors, so you relate what we do not relate!" — while you are calling him a liar.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿أَإِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ﴾ and ﴿إنَّنَا﴾: in the copies of the people of Syria it is ﴿إنَّنَا﴾.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "some of what you seek to hasten has drawn near to you". It is as though the lām came in because the meaning is "drew near", as the poet said: [138/a]
فقلت لها الحاجَاتُ يطرحن بالفتى * وهمٌّ تعَنّانى مُعَنّىً ركائبُهُ
(I said to her: needs fling a young man about, and a care has wearied me whose mounts are themselves wearied.)
He put the bāʾ on "the young man" because the meaning of ﴿يَطرحن﴾ is "they throw", and you say "I threw [with] the thing (ramaytu bi-l-shayʾ)" and "I flung it". The lām may be intrusive, the meaning being "radifakum" (has followed you), just as some of the Arabs said: "nafadhtu lahā miʾatan", meaning "nafadhtuhā miʾatan" (I paid her a hundred).

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ يَقُصُّ عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ أَكْثَرَ ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾: That is because the Children of Israel differed until some of them cursed others, so Allah said: this Qurʾān relates to them the guidance concerning what they differed over, if they would take it.

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَادِي ٱلْعُمْيِ عَن ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾: Had you said bi-hādin al-ʿumya [with tanwīn and the accusative], it would be correct. Ḥamza read (ومَا أنتَ تَهْدِى العُمْى عَن ضَلاَلتِهم), because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (وما إن تهدى العمى), which are two negatives combined, as the poet — Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma — said:
ما إن رَأيْتُ ولا سَمعتُ به * كاليوم طالِى أينْقُ جُرْبِ
(I have never seen nor heard of anyone like today's tar-smearer of mangy she-camels.)

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم﴾: its meaning is: when wrath becomes due upon them. It is like His saying ﴿حَقَّ عليهم القَوْلُ﴾ in another place. His saying ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةً مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾: the readers agree on the doubling of ﴿تكلّمهم﴾, and it is from speech (al-kalām). One of the ḥadīth transmitters told me that he said ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾ and ﴿تَكْلِمُهم﴾ ("it will wound them"). His saying (أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ) is read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads it with fatḥa makes the speaking fall upon it: ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ بأَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, and its position is accusative. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿بأن الناس﴾, and in the reading of Ubayy: (تُنَبِّئهم أنّ الناسَ); these two are evidence for whoever reads it with fatḥa. The people of Medina [read] ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾, so (إنَّ) is a new statement, yet it carries the meaning of the speech falling [on it]. Similar is ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسانُ إلى طعَامِهِ﴾: whoever says (أَنَّا) makes it genitive, referred back to "food": "to [the fact] that We poured down water"; and whoever reads it with kasra says: innā — He informed [them] of the cause of the food, how Allah decreed it.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ﴾: He did not say fa-yafzaʿu; He made faʿala (the past) refer back to yafʿalu (the imperfect). That is because in meaning it is: "and when the trumpet is blown, then [they] are terrified". Do you not see that your saying "I will stand on the day you stand" is like your saying "I will stand when you stand"? So it was answered with faʿala, because faʿala and yafʿalu are both sound with idhā. If you say: then where is the answer to His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾? I say: it may be in an implied faʿala with the wāw, as though He said: "and that is the day the trumpet is blown". And if you wish, you may say: its answer is left out, as He said ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إذ فَزِعُوا فَلاَ فَوْتَ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ يَرَى الذِينَ ظَلَموا﴾: its answer has been left out. And Allah knows best.
His saying ﴿وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ﴾: the readers lengthen the alif [ātūhu], meaning: "fāʿilūhu" (coming to Him). Ḥamza shortened it. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: a number of people related to me, among them al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, Qays and Abū Bakr, all of them from Jaḥsh ibn Ziyād al-Ḍabbī, from Tamīm ibn Ḥadhlam, who said: I recited to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd (وَكُلٌّ آتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ) with the alif lengthened, and he said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ﴾ without lengthening the alif. It is a good reading, referred back to His saying ﴿فَفَزِع﴾, as you say in ordinary speech: "he saw me and was terrified, and came back abased". Referring faʿala to its like is more pleasing to me, together with the reading of ʿAbd Allāh. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to me from al-Aʿmash from Tamīm from ʿAbd Allāh the like of the report of Abū Bakr and his companions.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ آمِنُونَ﴾: The reading of the readers is with the genitive construct; they said ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ [Translator's note: the two forms are identical in the source as printed; the intended contrast is evidently between fazaʿi yawmiʾidhin and yawmaʾidhin]. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read, in a chain of transmission part of which is part of what I related to you: (مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ); Tamīm recited it to them thus: (وَهُمْ من فَزَعٍ يَوْمِئذٍ), and he [Ibn Masʿūd] took it with tanwīn and the accusative. The genitive construct is more pleasing to me — even though I read with the accusative — because it is a known terror; do you not see that He said (لاَ يَحْزُنُهُمْ الفَزَعُ الأَكْبَرُ) and made it [139/a] definite? So annexing it, so that it becomes definite, is more pleasing to me. And it is correct.

farraa:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾: In one of the two readings: (وَأَنِ اتْلُ), without the wāw, in the jussive as a command. The wāw has been dropped from it because of the jussive as a command, as He said ﴿قُلْ إنّى أُمِرْت أَنْ أَكُون أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾: He made the wāw, with the prohibition, refer back to a word put in the accusative by an, because the meaning comes with (أمرت) in both ways together. Do you not see that you say: "I ordered ʿAbd Allāh that he should stand (an yaqūma)" and "that: stand! (wa-an qum)"? Allah said ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالمينَ وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاَة﴾, and this is like His saying ﴿وَأَنْ أَتْلُو القرآنَ﴾.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: His words «ولوطًا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) "اذكر" (remember), and the implied clause is resumptive. «إذ»: badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «لوطًا», and the clause «قال» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «وأنتم تبصرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تأتون».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرجال». «شهوة»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The clause «أئنكم لتأتون» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech, and the clause «بل أنتم قوم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «فما كان» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar is the ism (subject) of kāna, and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). The clause «إنهم أناس» is resumptive, and the clause «يتطهرون» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «فأنجيناه» is resumptive, and «أهله» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ in «أنجيناه». The clause «قدَّرناها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «امرأته».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «مطرًا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «فساء مطر» is resumptive, and the specified one (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e. "their rain".

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «سلام»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is a supplication. «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of «عباده». «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, i.e. "their associating". The clause «آلله خير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, for digression (iḍrāb). «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "كَمَنْ لم يخلق" (like one who did not create). «ذات»: naʿt (adjective). The clause «ما كان لكم ...» is a naʿt of «حدائق», and the interpreted maṣdar «أن تُنْبتوا» is the ism (subject) of kāna. The clause «أإله مع الله» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «بل هم قوم»; the clause «يعدلون» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, for digression (iḍrāb). «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "كمن لم يجعل" (like one who did not make). «خلالها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object, and likewise «لها».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "كَمَنْ لا يجيب" (like one who does not answer). «إذا»: an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يجيب». «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). «ما»: redundant (zāʾida). The clause «تذكَّرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "كَمَنْ لا يهديكم" (like one who does not guide you). The second «مَنْ»: a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding «مَنْ». «بشرًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرياح. «بين»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرًا». «يدي»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with yāʾ because it is a dual. The clause «تعالى الله» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "كَمَنْ لا يبدأ" (like one who does not originate). The second «مَنْ» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding «مَنْ». «هاتوا»: an inflexible (jāmid) imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause). «الغيب» is badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion), and the pronoun is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "their unseen". «إلا»: for restriction (ḥaṣr). «الله»: fāʿil (agent), i.e. none knows the unseen of those in the heavens and the earth except Allah. «أيان»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to «يبعثون». The clause «يبعثون» is the mafʿūl bihi of «يشعرون», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by «أيان» and carries the meaning of يعرفون (they know).

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «بل»: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). The preposition «في الآخرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ادَّارك», and the clause after «بل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "shall we be brought out when we are…". «آباؤنا» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun «نا». The clause «أئنا لمخرجون» is explicative of the implied apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: «هذا»: second object. «نحن»: tawkīd (emphasis) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «وعدنا». «وآباؤنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun «نا». «إن» is negating, and «هذا أساطير» are mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). The clause «إن هذا إلا أساطير» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «كيف كان» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative and carries the meaning of knowing. «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: His words «مما»: composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and the relative «ما»; the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ضَيْق».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: «متى»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). «هذا»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الوعد» is a badal (substitute). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: «عسى»: a complete (tāmm) past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is the interpreted maṣdar. The ism (subject) of «يكون» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). «رَدِف» has been made to include the meaning of قَرُبَ (drew near), and the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. «بعض»: fāʿil of «رَدِف». The clause «ردف لكم بعض» is the khabar (predicate) of «يكون».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The clause «وإن ربك لذو» is resumptive, and the clause of correction (istidrāk) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The negative clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إن ربك ...». «ما» is negating and inoperative (muhmala). «غائبة»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «في السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «غائبة». «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). The preposition «في كتاب» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «غائبة», and «إلا» is for restriction.

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: «الذي»: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The preposition «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يختلفون».

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The clause «وإنه لهدى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «وهو العزيز» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يقضي».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: «الدعاء»: second object. «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied apodosis (jawāb). «مُدْبرين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, and the clause «ولَّوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: «ما» operates like laysa, and the bāʾ in its khabar (predicate) is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «هادي» in the sense of "turning away". «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «وما أنت بهادي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ}. The clause «إن تسمع» is resumptive, and the clause «فهم مسلمون» is conjoined to the clause «يؤمن».

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The preposition «من الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «دابة», and the clause «تكلمهم» is a naʿt of «دابة». The interpreted maṣdar «أن الناس كانوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ).

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: The wāw is resumptive. «يوم»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) "اذكر" (remember). The preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فوجا». The preposition «ممن» is a badal (substitute) from «من كل», attached to what it is attached to. The clause «فهم يُوزعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نحشر».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya). «أمَّا» is composed of the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) «أم» and the interrogative (ما), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a relative noun, its khabar (predicate). The clause «أم ماذا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The clause «ووقع» is resumptive. «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وقع». The clause «فهم لا ينطقون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of رأى. The second object of جعل is omitted, i.e. "dark" (مظلمًا). The interpreted maṣdar «ليسكنوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلنا». «والنهار»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الليل», and «مبصرًا» is a noun conjoined to the implied «مظلمًا». The preposition «لقوم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «لآيات», and the clause «يؤمنون» is a naʿt of «لقوم».

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: His words «ويوم»: the wāw is a conjunction; «يوم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يوم» in verse (83). The preposition «في الصور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). «إلا» is for exception, and «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the excepted. The wāw in «وكل» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause «وكل أتوه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَن في السماوات والأرض». «داخرين»: ḥāl from the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: The clause «وترى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {يُنْفَخُ}. The clause «تحسبها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ترى», and the clause «وهي تمر» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جامدة». «صُنْعَ»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "صُنِعَتْ صُنْعَ" (it was made with the making of), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: «مَنْ»: conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «وهم آمِنون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «جاء». The tanwīn in «إذٍ» is compensation for a clause, i.e. "on the day when he comes with the good deed".

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «فَكُبَّتْ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with «قد» implied with it. The preposition «في النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كُبَّتْ». The clause «هل تجزون» is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied "saying". «ما»: a relative noun, second object of «تجزون».

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن أعبد» is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ). «هذه»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «الذي»: naʿt (adjective) of «رب». The wāw in «وله» is parenthetical, and the clause «وله كل شيء» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «اهتدى» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: The clause «سيريكم» is resumptive, within the scope of the speech, and the clause «وما ربك بغافل» is resumptive; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like laysa. The clause «وقل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ} in verse (91), and the preposition «عمَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) غافل.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «هدى»: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. The preposition «للمؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرى».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «وهم يوقنون» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause); the second «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first; the preposition «بالآخرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يوقنون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «فهم يعمهون» is conjoined to the clause «زيَّنَّا».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «أولئك الذين» is a second khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause «لهم سوء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal relative noun. The second «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, and the clause «وهم الأخسرون» is conjoined to the clause «لهم سوء».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «إنك لتلقى» is resumptive. «لدن» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تُلَقَّى». «عليم» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «حكيم».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied اذكر (remember), and the clause «قال» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «سآتيكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «نارًا». The two preposition and its genitive nouns «منها بخبر» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «آتيكم». The clause «أو آتيكم» is conjoined to the clause «سآتيكم». «قبس» is a badal (substitute) of «شهاب», and the clause «لعلكم تصطلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «لما» is a particle of necessity upon necessity (wujūb li-wujūb). «أنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and so is the clause with it. The preposition «في النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The wāw in «وسبحان» is resumptive, and «سبحان» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); «رب» is a badal (substitute); and «العالمين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The hāʾ in «إنه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The clause «أنا الله» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنه»; «العزيز الحكيم» are two naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «وألق عصاك» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ}. The conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «تهتز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «رآها», and the clause «كأنها جان» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «تهتز». «مدبرا» is a ḥāl that emphasizes its governor. The clause «ولم يعقِّب» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) «ولَّى». The clause «يا موسى» is resumptive, and the clause «إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون» is resumptive within the scope of the response to the vocative. «لديَّ» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, attached to the verb, and the second yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «إلا» is for disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the excepted (mustathnā). «حسنًا» is the object of «بدّل»; «بعد» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بدَّل». The clause «فإني غفور» is resumptive; «رحيم» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «تخرج» is the apodosis of an implied condition. «بيضاء» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تخرج», and the preposition «من غير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second ḥāl of the fāʿil of «تخرج». The preposition «في تسع» is attached to an implied verb, i.e. اذهب (go), and likewise «إلى فرعون». The clause «إنهم كانوا قومًا فاسقين» is a ḥāl of Pharaoh and his people.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «مبصرة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «آياتنا».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «وجحدوا» is conjoined to the clause {قَالُوا}; «ظُلْمًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «فانظر» is resumptive; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar (predicate) of kāna; and the clause «كان» is an object of the [verb of] looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, which carries the sense of knowing.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ولقد آتينا» is resumptive; «علمًا» is the second object. The clause «وقالا» is conjoined to the clause «آتينا». «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name; the preposition «من عباده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «كثير».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «وورث سليمان» is conjoined to the clause {وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا}; «الناس» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أوتينا». The clause «إن هذا لهو الفضل» is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa) between the two conjoined elements, and the clause «لهو الفضل» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «وحشر» is conjoined to the clause {وَقَالَ}; the preposition «من الجن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «جنوده»; the clause «فهم يوزعون» is conjoined to the clause «حُشر».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya). The yāʾ was dropped from «واد» in the script, following its pronunciation. «النمل» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause «لا يحطمنكم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; «لا» is prohibitive; it is a prohibition addressed to the troops in wording and to the ants in meaning. The clause «وهم لا يشعرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of Solomon and his troops.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فتبسَّم» is resumptive; «ضاحكًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «تبسَّم», and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تبسَّم». «رب» is a vocative (munādā) in a genitive construct, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ. «أن» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), putting the verb in the subjunctive, and the interpreted maṣdar is the second object of «أوزعني». The preposition and its genitive noun «وعلى والديَّ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ in «عليّ», with repetition of the preposition, and is attached to what that is attached to. «صالحًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «ترضاه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «صالحًا». The preposition «في عبادك» is attached to the verb, and «الصالحين» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وتفقَّد» is resumptive. «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause «لا أرى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the yāʾ in «لي». «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause «كان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «لأعذبنه» is the response to an implied oath. «عذابًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar being تعذيبًا.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The fāʾ in «فمكث» is resumptive. «غير» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), i.e. مكث وقتًا غير بعيد (he stayed a time not long). The preposition «بنبإ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «جئتك».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «تملكهم» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «وأوتيت» is conjoined to the clause «تملكهم». The nominal clause «ولها عرش» is conjoined to the verbal clause «أوتيت». The preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أوتيت».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «وجدتها» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the verb means «لقي» (to find, meet) and so takes a single object. «وقومها» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ in «وجدتها». The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الشمس». The clause «يسجدون» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «وجدتها» and what follows it. The clause «وزيَّن لهم الشيطان» is conjoined to the clause «يسجدون», and the clause «فهم لا يهتدون» is conjoined to the clause «صدَّهم».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «أن» puts the verb in the subjunctive, and the interpreted maṣdar is a badal (substitute) of {أَعْمَالَهُمْ}; the implied sense is: وزيَّن لهم الشيطان عدم السجود لله (and Satan made attractive to them not prostrating to Allah). The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الخبء».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause of transcendence is the khabar (predicate); «ربُّ» is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «صدقت» is the object of «ننظر», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative that carries the sense of knowing. «أم» is a conjunction, and the clause «كنت» is conjoined to the clause «صدقت».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «اذهب» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. «هذا» is a demonstrative, a naʿt (adjective) interpreted as a derived word, i.e. المشار إليه (the one pointed to). The hāʾ in «ألقه» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it was given sukūn for lightness, and this is a dialect usage. «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a relative noun, its khabar (predicate); and the clause «ماذا يرجعون» is a mafʿūl bihi of the [verb of] looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «إني ألقي» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; «الملأ» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «إنه من سليمان» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «وإنه بسم ...» is conjoined to the resumptive clause. The preposition and its genitive noun «بسم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. ابتدائي كائن (my beginning is [with]). The clause «ابتدائي باسم الله» is the khabar of «إنَّ», and «الرحمن الرحيم» are two naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «أن» puts the verb in the subjunctive. «مسلمين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «ائتوني». The interpreted maṣdar from «أنْ» and what follows it is a badal (substitute) of {كِتَابٌ}, as though it were said: أُلقي إليَّ: ألا تعلُوا عليّ (there has been delivered to me: that you not exalt yourselves against me).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «ما كنت» is resumptive; «أمرًا» is the object of «قاطعة». «تشهدون» is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by a necessarily implied «أن», the sign of its subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «أولو»: a khabar (predicate), nominative with wāw, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. The clause «والأمر إليك» is conjoined to the clause «نحن أولو», and the clause «فانظري» is conjoined to the clause «الأمر إليك». «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a relative noun, the khabar; and the clause «ماذا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the [verb of] looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, which carries the sense of knowing.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The conditional clause and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of inna; «أذلة» is the second object. The wāw in «وكذلك» is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), [followed by] a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «يفعلون» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The implied sense is: يفعلون فِعْلا مثل ذلك الفعل (they do a doing like that doing).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «وإني مرسلة» is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). The two preposition and its genitive nouns «إليهم بهدية» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مرسلة». As for «بم»: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to «يرجع»; the alif of the interrogative «ما» was dropped because it is in the genitive. «فناظرة» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «مرسلة». The clause «يرجع» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «ناظرة», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative that carries the sense of knowing.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, as is the clause «فما آتاني الله خير». «ما» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خير» is its khabar (predicate). «آتاني» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied fatḥa because of impossibility [of pronouncing it]; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «ممَّا» is composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and the relative «ما», and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير». The preposition «بهديتكم» is attached to «تفرحون», and the clause «بل أنتم تفرحون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «ارجع» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; the oath clause and its response are conjoined to the clause «ارجع». The preposition «بجنود» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «نأتينَّهم», and the clause «لا قِبل لهم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنود». The preposition «بها» is attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached. «أذلة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ, and the clause «وهم صاغرون» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «نخرجنَّهم».
