2- Man plots; as for Allah, He does not plot. Plotting was attributed to Allah only for the sake of mushākala (correspondence), which is one of the devices of rhetoric that we have alluded to before. The definition of mushākala: it is mentioning a thing by the word for something else because it occurs in its company.
[Translator's note: the numbering of the Benefits (3, then 1, 2) is as in the source.]

safi-cedvel:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لوطا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; (إذ) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb [Note: or a badal (substitute) of (لوطا), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), in the sense of what Lūṭ said at that time.]; (لقومه) is attached to (قال); (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; (الواو) is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial) ...
The clause «(اذكر) لوطا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تأتون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
(55) (الهمزة) is mentioned to reinforce the disapproval; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (شهوة) is an accusative ḥāl of الرجال; (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent); (بل) is for digression (iḍrāb) and commencement ...
The clause إنّكم لتأتون ... has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a badal of the clause تأتون الفاحشة ...].
The clause «تأتون الرجال ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أنتم قوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تجهلون ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
The clause «أنتم تبصرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تبصرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) أنتم.

* Benefits:
From the stories of the Qur'an: «the story of Lūṭ» ...
Ibrāhīm departed from Egypt, taking Lūṭ with him on his journey, and they returned from that land with much wealth and abundant good, and settled in that Holy Land. But it became too narrow for their livestock and flocks, so Lūṭ moved away from the encampment of his uncle Ibrāhīm, and settled in the city of Sodom.
Its people were of corrupt morals and evil intentions; they did not refrain from disobedience, nor did they forbid one another from wrongdoing ... They invented an abomination in which none had preceded them: they used to come to males, and leave the women whom Allah had created for them.
[Translator's note: the source prints «الذاكران» here; in the repeated text under āyas 57-58 it reads «الذكران» (males), which is the sense translated.]
Allah revealed to Lūṭ that he should call them to the worship of Allah and that they should abandon the abominations they practised. But they put their fingers in their ears; their insight had been blinded and rust had been cast upon their hearts. They made threats to Lūṭ and those who believed with him, and resolved to drive them out of their town.
[Translator's note: the source here prints «فواعدوا» ("they made an appointment with"); the parallel text under āyas 57-58 has «فتوعدوا» ("they threatened"), which is the sense translated.]
Lūṭ asked his Lord to help him against these sinful people and to bring painful punishment upon them.
Allah answered his prayer and sent angels to this town whose people were wrongdoers, to bring upon them the worst of punishment. The messengers passed by Ibrāhīm first, told him of their mission and gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.
Ibrāhīm feared for Lūṭ and those who believed with him, but the messengers reassured him and told him that Lūṭ and those who believed with him would not be struck by the punishment, and would be among those saved.
The messengers came to stay at Lūṭ's house, and the people heard of these guests who had come to Lūṭ's house. The angels were in the form of young men of the freshest build and the most beautiful faces, so Lūṭ's people coveted them and surrounded Lūṭ's house, wanting to reach his guests.
A cloud of grief covered Lūṭ, and a storm of anger seized him, as he saw the people storming his house and trying to assault his guests.
When the angels saw the grief and distress Lūṭ was in, they calmed his anxiety and stilled his fear, and said: O Lūṭ, we are the messengers of your Lord; we have come to rescue you and to repel the aggression from you, so these unbelievers will not reach you.
They commanded him to travel by night with his family, and to leave this town which Allah had decreed He would turn upside down.
Lūṭ went out with his family, and left the town and its people without regret for it. Then the command of Allah came to it: its land was shaken, it was turned upside down, and then it was covered with a rain of baked clay (sijjīl), so that their abode became a barren waste, and their houses empty because of their wrongdoing «إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ».
Part Twenty
Remainder of Sūrat al-Naml
From āya 56 to āya 93; Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, its āyas are 88; Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt from āya 1 to āya 45

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (ما) is negating; (جواب) is the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن قالوا ...) is in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان.
من قريتكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخرجوا).
The clause «ما كان جواب..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أخرجوا..» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّهم أناس ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يتطهّرون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أناس.

safi-cedvel:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (أهله) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object pronoun in (أنجيناه); (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (امرأته) is accusative as the excepted, in a discontinuous or a continuous exception; (من الغابرين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قدّرناها).
The clause «أنجيناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قدّرناها ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(58) (الواو) is a conjunction; (عليهم) is attached to (أمطرنا); (مطرا) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: in the sense of stones or instruments of punishment ... or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun).]; (الفاء) is resumptive; (ساء) is a past verb for expressing blame ...
The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "مطرهم".
The clause «أمطرنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ساء مطر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Benefits:
- From the stories of the Qur'an: «the story of Lūṭ»:
Ibrāhīm departed from Egypt, taking Lūṭ with him on his journey, and they returned from that land with much wealth and abundant good, and settled in that Holy Land. But it became too narrow for their livestock and flocks, so Lūṭ moved away from the encampment of his uncle Ibrāhīm, and settled in the city of Sodom.
Its people were of corrupt morals and evil intentions; they did not refrain from disobedience, nor did they forbid one another from wrongdoing. They invented an abomination in which none had preceded them: they used to come to males, and leave the women whom Allah had created for them. Allah revealed to Lūṭ that he should call them to the worship of Allah and that they should abandon the abominations they practised. But they put their fingers in their ears; their eyes had been blinded, and rust had been cast upon their hearts.
They threatened Lūṭ and those who believed with him, and resolved to drive them out of their town.
Lūṭ asked his Lord to help him against these sinful people and to bring painful punishment upon them.
Allah answered his prayer and sent angels to this town whose people were wrongdoers, to bring upon them the worst of punishment. The messengers passed by Ibrāhīm first, told him of their mission and gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.
Ibrāhīm feared for Lūṭ and those who believed with him, but the messengers reassured him and informed him that Lūṭ and those who believed with him would not be struck by the punishment, and would be among those saved. The messengers came to stay at Lūṭ's house.
The people heard of these guests who had come to Lūṭ's house. The angels were in the form of young men of the freshest build and the most beautiful faces, so Lūṭ's people coveted them and surrounded Lūṭ's house, wanting to reach his guests.
A cloud of grief covered Lūṭ, and a storm of anger seized him, as he saw the people storming his house and trying to assault his guests.
When the angels saw the grief and distress Lūṭ was in, they calmed his anxiety and stilled his fear, and said: O Lūṭ, we are the messengers of your Lord; we have come to rescue you and to repel the aggression from you, so these unbelievers will not reach you. They commanded him to travel by night with his family, and to leave this town which Allah had decreed He would turn upside down.
Lūṭ went out with his family, and left the town and its people without regret for it. Then the command of Allah came to it: its land was shaken, it was turned upside down, and then it was covered with a rain of baked clay (sijjīl), so that their abode became a barren waste, and their houses empty because of their wrongdoing «إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ».
[Translator's note: this story repeats, almost word for word, the one given in the source under āyas 54-55.]

safi-cedvel:59-64.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الحمد; (الواو) is a conjunction; (سلام) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: what permitted beginning with it, although it is indefinite, is that it denotes praise.]; (على عباده) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of عباده; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative; (أم) is the connected (muttaṣila) one, a conjunction; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the resumptive pronoun being omitted.] ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما يشركون) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, which is the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "their associating".
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الحمد لله» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «سلام على عباده ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «اصطفى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين), the resumptive pronoun being omitted.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
(60) (أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل plus the hamza; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted, its implied form being "كمن لم يخلق" ("like one who does not create") ... [Note: the khabar has been reconstructed in other ways according to the sense, i.e.: "يكفر بنعمته ويشرك به" ("is his favour denied and others associated with him"), or ...
"خير أم ما يشركون" ("better, or what they associate") ... etc.]; (لكم) is attached to (أنزل); (من السماء) is attached to (أنزل); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (به) is attached to (أنبت), the bāʾ being causal; (ذات) is an accusative naʿt of حدائق [Note: it is singular because the qualified noun is a non-rational plural.]; (ما) is negating; (لكم) is attached to the khabar of كان; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنبتوا ...) is in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان.
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval; (إله) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: an indefinite noun supported by the interrogative.]; (مع) is an accusative adverb attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ إله; (بل) is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī).
The clause «من خلق ... (كمن لم يخلق) ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق السموات» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «أنزل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أنبتنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أنزل; in the first-person pronoun there is iltifāt (a shift of person).
The clause «ما كان لكم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of حدائق [Note: it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of حدائق, since it has become specified by the description.].
The clause «تنبتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أإله مع الله» has no grammatical position: a resumption.
The clause «هم قوم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption.
The clause «يعدلون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of قوم.
(61) (أم) in the four places is like the preceding (أم); (من جعل) is like من خلق; (قرارا) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعل; (خلالها) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second object whose governor is the second جعل; (لها) is the second object whose governor is the third جعل; (بين) is an accusative adverb attached to the second object whose governor is the fourth جعل; (أإله مع الله) is like the first; (بلى) is like the first; (لا) is negating ...
[Translator's note: the source writes «بلى», but the word in the āya is بَلْ.]
The clause «من جعل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعل الأرض ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «جعل ... أنهارا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جعل ... رواسي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جعل ... حاجزا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أإله مع الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).
(62) (أم من يجيب ...) is like أم من خلق; (إذا) is an adverb of future time, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to (يجيب); (خلفاء) is the second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يجعلكم; (أإله مع الله) is like the first; (قليلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, its governor being تذكّرون; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the paucity.
The clause «من يجيب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يجيب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «دعاه ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يكشف ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يجعلكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أإله مع الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تذكّرون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(63) (أم من يهديكم) is like أم من خلق ...; (في ظلمات) is attached to (يهديكم); (من يرسل ...) is like من يهديكم and conjoined to it; (بشرا) is an accusative ḥāl of الرياح; (بين) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (بشرا) [Note: i.e. before the rain.]; (عما) is attached to (تعالى), and ما is a maṣdar-forming particle.
The clause «من يهديكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يهديكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يرسل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the (second) relative (من).
The clause «أإله مع الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعالى الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
(64) (أم من يبدأ ...) is like أم من خلق; (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (من يرزقكم) is like من يبدأ and conjoined to it; (من السماء) is attached to (يرزقكم); (هاتوا) is a non-inflecting (jāmid) imperative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn [Note: it has neither an imperfect nor a past.], by analogy with its counterpart predicated of the wāw of the group; (كنتم) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (صادقين) is the accusative khabar of كنتم, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يبدأ الخلق ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يعيده ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يرزقكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «أإله مع الله» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هاتوا برهانكم» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(60) حدائق: plural of حديقة, a noun for a garden with a wall around it; its pattern is فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة, because the wall surrounds (aḥdaqa) it.
(بهجة): a noun from (بهجه) meaning "he gladdened him", of the فتح class; it means beauty and freshness; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(61) حاجزا: active participle of the triliteral حجز; its pattern is فاعل.
(62) المضطر: passive participle of the five-letter اضطرّ; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, and it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the tāʾ by ṭāʾ ... see āya (126) of Sūrat al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person): in the words of Allah the Exalted فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ.
A shift from the third person to the first person with the nūn of majesty, to emphasise that the action belongs exclusively — by way of contrast — to Him the Exalted Himself, and to announce that causing these gardens to grow, varied in kinds, qualities, colours, tastes, scents and shapes — with the consummate beauty and splendid radiance they possess — by a single water, is a mighty matter that none can accomplish but He alone, Mighty and Majestic.

* Benefits:
- The interrogative hamza:
We have spoken previously about some of the characteristics of the interrogative hamza, and here we shall complete the study of this hamza: it is the root of the interrogative particles; indeed it is — as Sībawayh said — "the interrogative particle that does not leave it for something else, and the interrogative originally has no other". They only left out the interrogative hamza in «من، ومتى، وهل» and the like because they were safe from ambiguity. For this reason it is distinguished by special rulings. The first of them: it may be omitted, whether it precedes «أم», as in the words of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فوالله ما أدري وإن كنت داريا ... بسبع رمين الجمر أم بثمان
(By Allah, I do not know — though I am one who knows — whether they cast the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
He meant: أبسبع.
or does not precede أم, as in the words of al-Kumayt:
طربت وما شوقا إلى البيض أطرب ... ولا لعبا مني وذو الشيب يلعب
(I was moved — yet not out of longing for the fair ones am I moved, nor in play; and does the grey-haired man play?)
The second: it is used to request a conception (taṣawwur), e.g.:
«أخالد مقبل أم علي» ("Is it Khālid who is coming, or ʿAlī?").
And to request an assent (taṣdīq), e.g. «أمحمد قادم»؟ ("Is Muḥammad coming?"). The rest of the interrogative particles are restricted to requesting assent only.
[Translator's note: as printed; the usual statement in the grammar books is that هل alone is restricted to requesting assent, while the other interrogative nouns request conception.]
The third: it enters upon the affirmative, as already mentioned, and upon the negative, e.g. «أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ».
The fourth: its complete priority of position (taṣdīr): it is not mentioned after «أم», so we do not say: أقرأ خالد أم أكتب؟
But we say: أقرأ خالد أم هل كتب؟ ("Did Khālid read, or did he write?"). Likewise it precedes the conjunctions «الواو، أو الفاء، أو ثمّ», to draw attention to its being original in taking the first position, as in:
«أولم ينظروا» «أفلم يسيروا» «أثمّ إذا ما وقع آمنتم به»; whereas its sisters come after the conjunctions, e.g. «وكيف تفكرون، فأين تذهبون، فأنى تؤفكون، فأي الفريقين».
The fifth: the interrogative hamza differs from the others in many matters, and what is permitted with it is not permitted with the others:
1- An accusative noun may come after it, e.g. أعبد الله ضربته ("Is it ʿAbd Allāh whom you struck?") and أعمرا قتلت أخاه ("Is it ʿAmr whose brother you killed?"); in this case you imply a verb between the hamza and the accusative noun; and likewise: أزيدا مررت به أم عمرا ("Is it Zayd you passed by, or ʿAmr?").
2- The interrogative hamza entering upon the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl): when the interrogative hamza enters upon the connecting hamza, the interrogative hamza remains and the connecting hamza falls away, because the interrogative hamza takes the place of the connecting hamza in enabling the pronunciation of the quiescent letter, e.g.: أبن زيد أنت؟ ("Are you the son of Zayd?")
And e.g. «أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعالِينَ» «أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ» «افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً». Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
فقالت أبن قيس ذا ... وبعض الشيب يعجبها
(She said: "Is this Ibn Qays?" — and some grey hair pleases her.)
3- The interrogative hamza and the oath:
You say «آلله», asking a question together with emphasis by oath, and likewise «ايم الله» and «ايمن الله»; the interrogative hamza takes the place of the wāw of the oath, and the thing sworn by is made genitive by it. Here the connecting hamza in the Name of Majesty, or in «ايم» or «ايمن», is not dropped, but is made into a madda; it is here just as it would be if it entered upon something other than an oath. So you say: «آلرجل فعل ذلك» ("Was it the man who did that?"). The interrogative hamza here carries two meanings: interrogation and standing in for the wāw of the oath. So if you say «آلله لتفعلنّ», it is as though you had said:
«أتقسم بالله لتفعلنّ» ("Do you swear by Allah that you will surely do it?").
4- The interrogative hamza entering upon the definite article «ال»: when the interrogative hamza enters upon the definite article, the first is kept as a hamza and the second is turned into a madda, as in your saying: «آلرجل قال ذاك» ("Was it the man who said that?"); in writing, the alif stands for the two hamzas, e.g. «آلساعة جئت» ("Is it now that you have come?"). Of this kind are the words of Allah the Exalted:
«آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ» «آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ» «آلْآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ».
5- The hamza departing from genuine interrogation:
The hamza departs from genuine interrogation and is used for eight meanings.
a- Equivalence (taswiya): سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ.
b- Invalidating disapproval (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): e.g.: أَشَهِدُوا خَلْقَهُمْ؟ أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ؟
c- Rebuking disapproval (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ؟
d- Affirmation (taqrīr): e.g. أنصرت بكرا and أبكرا نصرت؟ ("Did you help Bakr?" / "Is it Bakr you helped?") e- Mockery (tahakkum), e.g.: قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا؟
And command, e.g.: «أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ», i.e. "submit!".
g- Wonder (taʿajjub), e.g.: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ.
h- Finding something slow (istibṭāʾ), e.g.: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟
i- Iltifāt in His saying: «فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ» after His saying «أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً»: in conveying the report He moved from the third person to speaking of Himself in the first person in His saying فأنبتنا. The secret of this is to emphasise that the action of causing growth belongs exclusively to Him the Exalted Himself, and to announce that causing gardens of different kinds to grow, with the ornaments of colour, the beauties of form, the varied tastes and the different scents of varying fragrance and perfume that appear in them — none of this can be accomplished except by an Able Creator, and He is Allah alone. For this reason He reinforced this exclusiveness by saying afterwards «ما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُنْبِتُوا شَجَرَها».
[Translator's note: the source announces eight meanings but lists items a–i, of which "the command" has no letter (it would be "f", و) and item i (iltifāt) is not a meaning of the hamza but repeats the Rhetoric section above.]

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is negating; (من) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يعلم, in the position of the nominative [Note: it may be the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with (الغيب) a badal (substitute) of the relative noun, and the fāʿil of يعلم being the word] [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source; presumably "the word (lafẓ) of the Name of Majesty" is meant.]; (في السموات) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من; (الغيب) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi; (إلّا) is for exception, meaning غير ("other than") [Note: or a particle of exception meaning لكن ("but"), so that the exception is discontinuous, because a continuous exception would imply that Allah is among those in the heavens and the earth, i.e. that He has a place ... On this view the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "يعلم الغيب".]; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, and it together with the إلّا before it is a nominative naʿt (adjective) of the relative noun [Note: it may be a badal of the relative noun if إلّا is not taken to mean غير, i.e. "no one knows the unseen except Allah".]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أيّان) is an accusative adverb of time, its governor being (يبعثون), and the wāw in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما يشعرون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «يبعثون» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يشعرون, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative أيّان; it carries the sense of يعرفون ("they know").
(66) (بل) is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī) in the three places; (في الآخرة) is attached to (ادّارك); (في شكّ) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم); (منها) is attached to a naʿt of شكّ, and the second (منها) is attached to the khabar (عمون).
The clause «ادّارك علمهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم في شك منها ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم منها عمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:67-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of disapproval; (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb explained by what follows, i.e. "أنخرج إذا كنّا ..." ("shall we be brought out when we have become ..."); (الواو) is a conjunction; (آباؤنا) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the attached pronoun that is the noun of كان [Note: the conjoining without an emphasising detached pronoun is permitted because of the separator (ترابا).], nominative; (الهمزة) is like the first; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «قال الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The conditional clause — its protasis and its apodosis — is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كنّا..» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّا لمخرجون» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(68) (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath, and (نا) is a pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive (وعدنا); (هذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نحن) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun that is the nāʾib fāʿil; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the attached pronoun (نا), nominative; (قبل) is a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (وعدنا); (إن) is negating; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أساطير) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا).
The clause «وعدنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا أساطير ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سيروا); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (انظروا ... المجرمين): the i'rab of something similar has been given [Note: in āya (51) of this sūra, in Part Nineteen.].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سيروا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «انظروا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause سيروا.
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
(70) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is the prohibitive lā, governing the jussive; (عليهم) is attached to the negated (تحزن); (في ضيق) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of تكن; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. يمكرونه.], and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما يمكرون) is in the position of the genitive by (من), attached to ضيق.
The clause «لا تحزن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «لا تكن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «يمكرون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(ضيق): maṣdar of ضاق, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (متى) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا); (الوعد) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) —, nominative; (كنتم) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «متى هذا الوعد ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كنتم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(عسى) is a complete (tāmm) past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكون ...); the noun of يكون is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (لكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ردف), by making it carry the sense of قرب ("drew near") [Note: or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and the second-person pronoun is its object ... In al-Qāmūs: ردفه, like سمع and نصر, means "he followed him".]; (بعض) is the nominative fāʿil of ردف; (الذي) is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi, in the position of the genitive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عسى أن يكون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «يكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ردف ... بعض ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of يكون.
The clause «تستعجلون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).

safi-cedvel:73-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (ذو) is a nominative khabar (predicate), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (على الناس) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) فضل; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating.
The clause «إنّ ربّك لذو..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا يشكرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
(74) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is like the first; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the resumptive pronoun being omitted; (الواو) is a conjunction; the second (ما) is like the first and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it ...
The clause «إنّ ربّك ليعلم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ ربّك لذو ...
The clause «يعلم..» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تكنّ صدورهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «يعلنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
75 (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (غائبة) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (في السماء) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of غائبة; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (في كتاب) is attached to the khabar of غائبة ...
The clause «ما من غائبة..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ ربّك لذو ...

* Morphology:
(غائبة): it has been said to be the active participle of the triliteral غاب, with the tāʾ added for intensiveness; it has been said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) like العاقبة and العافية; and it has been said to be a noun, not an adjective, like النطيحة and الذبيحة. The pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
- The kinds of tāʾ marbūṭa that attach to nouns:
a- It is a sign of the feminine, with rulings and details that we pass over for brevity, e.g. قائم and قائمة. Five patterns are excepted from taking this tāʾ:
1- فعول, e.g. امرأة جسور ("a bold woman") 2- فعيل, e.g. امرأة جريح ("a wounded woman") 3- مفعال, e.g. امرأة منحار ("a woman who slaughters much").
4- مفعيل, e.g. امرأة معطير ("a much-perfumed woman") 5- مفعل, e.g. امرأة مغشم ("a reckless woman"). In all these adjectives man and woman are alike in being without this tāʾ.
b- It is for separation (faṣl): the tāʾ of separation separates the singular from its genus, e.g. «ثمرة» ("a fruit"), and separates the genus from its singular, e.g. «كماة» ("truffles").
c- The tāʾ of compensation (ʿiwaḍ): it comes as compensation for the fāʾ of the noun when it is dropped, e.g. عدة, or its ʿayn, e.g. إقامة, or its lām, e.g. سنة.
d- The tāʾ of Arabicisation (taʿrīb): it comes in Arabicising foreign nouns.
e- The tāʾ of intensiveness (mubālagha): it attaches to an adjective to indicate intensiveness in it, e.g. راوية, نسّابة, علّامة, etc., for one who transmits much, one expert in genealogies, and one of much and abundant knowledge.

safi-cedvel:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(على بني) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقصّ), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, as it is attached (mulḥaq) to the masculine plural; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون).
The clause «إنّ هذا القرآن ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقصّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «هم فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يختلفون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم.
(77) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (للمؤمنين) is attached to (رحمة). The clause «إنّه لهدى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:78-81.t:
* I'rab:
(بينهم) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقضي); (بحكمه) is attached to (يقضي); (الواو) is a conjunction — or circumstantial —; (العليم) is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هو ...
The clause «إن ربّك يقتضي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
[Translator's note: the source prints «يقتضي»; the word in the āya is يَقْضِي.]
The clause «يقضي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «هو العزيز ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يقضي [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).].
(79) (الفاء) links to the apodosis of an implied condition; (على الله) is attached to (توكّل); (على الحقّ) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «توكّل ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want success, then put your trust ...".
The clause «إنّك على الحق ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(80) (لا) is negating in both places; (الدعاء) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the second verb تسمع, and that of the first was omitted because the second indicates it; (ولّوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (مدبرين) is a ḥāl that emphasises the content of the verb (ḥāl muʾakkida).
The clause «إنّك لا تسمع ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption containing a second reason for the trust.
The clause «لا تسمع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا تسمع (the second) ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first clause لا تسمع.
The clause «ولّوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(81) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating, functioning like ليس; (أنت) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of ما; (هادي) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما; (العمي) is a genitive muḍāf ilayhi; (عن ضلالتهم) is attached to هادي, by making it carry the sense of صارف ("turning away"); (إن) is negating; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (بآياتنا) is attached to (يؤمن); (الفاء) is causal.
The clause «ما أنت بهادي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنك لا تسمع.
The clause «إن تسمع إلّا من ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for what preceded.
The clause «يؤمن..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هم مسلمون» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Rhetoric:
Completion (al-tatmīm): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِذا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ».
The negation is restricted in order to complete the simile and emphasise the negation: for they — besides being deaf to the call to the truth — turn away from the caller, turning their backs; and there is no doubt that the deaf man does not hear the call even when the caller faces his ear-hole, close to him, so how much less when he is behind him or far from him?

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (عليهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وقع); (لهم) is attached to (أخرجنا); (من الأرض) is attached to the verb أخرجنا; (بآياتنا) is attached to the negated (يوقنون).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الناس كانوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (تكلّمهم), i.e. "بأنّ الناس".
The clause «وقع القول ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أخرجنا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تكلّمهم» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of دابّة.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The clause «لا يوقنون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
- The Beast of the Earth (dābbat al-arḍ):
We have no text that specifies for us its kind and nature, and all that is required of us is to believe in the unseen as He, Glorified and Exalted, has informed of it; He knows best about it. It does not harm us to be ignorant of it, just as it does not benefit us to run after knowledge of it. It is enough for us to say about it, and about similar hidden matters, «Allah knows best about that».

safi-cedvel:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أذكر"; (من كلّ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (فوجا); (ممن) is attached to what the prepositional phrase (من كلّ) is attached to, because it is a badal (substitute) of it; (بآياتنا) is attached to (يكذّب); (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the wāw in (يوزعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نحشر ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يكذّب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هم يوزعون» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نحشر.
The clause «يوزعون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (هم).
(84) (حتّى) is a particle of commencement (ibtidāʾ); (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproach; (بآياتي) is attached to (كذّبتم); (بها) is attached to (تحيطوا); (علما) is an accusative tamyīz (specification); (أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل; (ماذا) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تعملون [Note: or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) a relative noun, the khabar, with the clause كنتم تعملون as the ṣila of ذا.].
The clause «جاؤوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كذّبتم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لم تحيطوا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl [Note: the clause may be circumstantial, adding to the rebuke, i.e. "did you deny them without understanding them or reflecting on them?"].
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(فوج): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning a group; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; the plural is أفواج and فؤوج with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (عليهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وقع); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (الباء) is a preposition of causation; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما ظلموا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (وقع).
The clause «وقع القول ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «هم لا ينطقون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا ينطقون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of rebuke; (أنّا) is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its noun; (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (يسكنوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; (فيه) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسكنوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا جعلنا ...) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يروا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسكنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (جعلنا); the second object of جعلنا is omitted, its implied form being "مظلما" [Note: the verb (جعلنا) may mean "we created", in which case nothing need be supplied.].
(الواو) is a conjunction; (النهار مبصرا) are conjoined to the first and second objects [Note: or they are the two objects of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned, the conjoining then being of clauses.]; (في ذلك) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (اللام) is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis; (آيات) is the accusative noun of إنّ, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (لقوم) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعلنا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يسكنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يؤمنون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of قوم.

* Benefits:
1- We have seen that «جعل», in one of its two uses, puts two objects in the accusative. This āya contains both uses of جعل: in the words of Allah the Exalted أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ it puts a single object in the accusative, namely الليل — unless we consider that the clause «لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ» takes the place of the second object; and in the words of the Exalted وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً, النهار is the first object and «مبصرا» the second object ... i.e. «وجعلنا النهار مبصرا».
2- Al-Zamakhsharī says, describing some words that Allah attributes to Himself: "Do you not see His saying «صنع الله» and «وعد الله» and «فطرة الله» — after He has marked them, by annexing them to Himself, with the mark of magnification — how it is followed by His saying: «الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ», «وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً», and «لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ الْمِيعادَ», «لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ»."

safi-cedvel:87-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" [Note: or conjoined to the preceding adverb (يوم نحشر ...) in āya (83) of this sūra.]; (في الصور) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb ينفخ; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (في السموات) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من, and likewise (في الأرض) for the second relative noun; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the excepted, and the fāʿil (agent) of (شاء) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. Allah; (الواو) is circumstantial; (كلّ) is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: it indicates generality, and it is on the assumption of an implied muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. كلّهم.]; (داخرين) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of أتوه.
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ينفخ في الصور ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ...
The clause «فزع من ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ينفخ ...
The past verb has the force of the imperfect because its occurrence is certain.
The clause «شاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (من).
The clause «كلّ أتوه ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of those in the heavens and the earth.
The clause «أتوه ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ).
(88) (الواو) is a conjunction; (جامدة) is the second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تحسبها; (الواو) is circumstantial; (مرّ) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (صنع) is the accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تفعلونه.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تفعلون) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to خبير.
The clause «ترى ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ينفخ في الصور.
The clause «تحسبها ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ترى.
The clause «هي تمرّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in جامدة.
The clause «(صنعت) صنع ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أتقن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «إنّه خبير ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «تفعلون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
(89) (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (بالحسنة) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاء, i.e. "bringing it"; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (له) is attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ خير; (منها) is attached to خير; (الواو) is circumstantial; (من فزع) is attached to (آمنون); (يومئذ) is attached to (آمنون).
The clause «من جاء ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «جاء بالحسنة ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «له خير ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هم ... آمنون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: it may be conjoined to the resumptive clause, and so have no grammatical position.].
(90) (من جاء بالسيّئة) is like من جاء بالحسنة; (الفاء) links to the apodosis; (وجوههم) is the nominative nāʾib fāʿil of the verb كبّت; (في النار) is attached to (كبّت); (هل) is an interrogative particle used for negation, and (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تعملونه.
The clause «من جاء (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من جاء (the first).
The clause «جاء بالسيّئة ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «كبّت وجوههم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هل تجزون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is a ḥāl of the pronoun in وجوههم [Note: because the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi.].
The clause «كنتم تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(88) جامدة: feminine of جامد, the active participle of the triliteral جمد; its pattern is فاعل, and it is فاعلة.
(مرّ): maṣdar of the triliteral مرّ, of the نصر class; and there are two other maṣdars, namely مرور but He turned to the past tense to convey that the terror is certain and established, that it will come to pass without doubt, befalling the people of the heavens and the earth, because the past verb indicates the existence of the action and that it is a certainty.
[Translator's note: the text is disjointed in the source: only one of the "two other maṣdars" is named, and the sentence then continues with a rhetorical remark that belongs to the past verb فَفَزِعَ in āya 87. No «Rhetoric» heading precedes the following paragraph in the source.]
Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَتَرَى الْجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ.
A wondrous antithesis between stillness and rapid motion: He made what appears to the eye of the beholder like the mountain in its stillness and firmness, yet it is swift, passing along rapidly as the clouds pass. Such is the case of great bodies, numerous in number: when they move, their motion can scarcely be discerned.
Al-Zamakhsharī described these āyas eloquently, saying:
"Look at the eloquence of this speech, the beauty of its composition and arrangement, the firmness of its binding, the soundness of its explanation, and how each part takes hold of the waistband of another, as though it had been cast in a single mould. For some reason it has overwhelmed every power and silenced the most eloquent tongues. When a maṣdar like this comes after a piece of speech, it comes like a witness to its truth and a herald of its rightness, and to the fact that it could not have been otherwise than as it was."

* Benefits:
- مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْها: it is noticeable in this āya and in the one after it that the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) comes joined with the fāʾ, because the apodosis is a nominal clause. This invites us to repeat the cases in which the apodosis is joined with the fāʾ; someone has spared us the trouble by collecting them in this verse of poetry, saying:
اسمية طلبية وبجامد ... وبما ولن وقد وبالتسويف
(A nominal clause, a clause of request, and with a non-inflecting verb, and with ما, لن, قد and with the particle of futurity.)

safi-cedvel:91-92.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is the restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); (التاء) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أعبد) is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being أمرت.
(هذه) is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (البلدة) is a genitive badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ربّ; (الواو) is parenthetical; (له) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) كلّ; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أن أكون) is like أن أعبد; (من المسلمين) is attached to the omitted khabar of أكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون) is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi, its governor being the second أمرت.
The clause «أمرت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: it may be in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of an implied verb of saying, i.e. "say to them: إنّما ..."].
The clause «أعبد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «حرّمها ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «له كلّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «أمرت (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أمرت (the first).
The clause «أكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
(92) (الواو) is a conjunction; (أن أتلو) is like أن أعبد; (الفاء) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (اهتدى) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied fatḥa, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّما) is like the first; (لنفسه) is attached to (يهتدي); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من ضلّ) is like من اهتدى; (الفاء) links to the apodosis; (إنّما) is like the first; (من المنذرين) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أتلو ...) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون).
The clause «أتلو ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third particle-relative (أن).
The clause «من اهتدى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اهتدى ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّما يهتدي ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من ضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من اهتدى.
The clause «ضلّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «قل ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنا من المنذرين ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl, and the link with the condition is implied, i.e. "say to him".

* Rhetoric:
Precaution (al-iḥtirās): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَلَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ:
A beautiful precaution. This device has been mentioned before: it is brought to ward off a misconception that the speech might give rise to. He, Glorified be He, connected His name with Makka to honour it and to mention its sanctity; and when He had connected His name with the town singled out for this honour, He followed this by attributing everything other than it to His dominion, to cut off the misconception that His dominion is restricted to the town referred to, and to draw attention to the fact that the first attribution was intended only for honour, not because it alone is the property of Allah the Exalted.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (لله) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الحمد; (السين) is a particle of futurity; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is negating, functioning like ليس; (غافل) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما; the second (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted, i.e. تعملونه.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تعملون) is in the position of the genitive by (عن), attached to (mutaʿalliq) غافل.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّما أمرت [Note: in āya (91) of this sūra.].
The clause «الحمد لله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «سيريكم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تعرفونها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سيريكم.
The clause «ما ربّك بغافل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).

* Benefits:
- At the close of Sūrat al-Naml we refer the reader to what al-Bāqillānī said in interpreting and analysing this sūra and the places of inimitability in it; he said about it what is fine to say, even though no one of power or might can attain the eloquence of the Qur'an. Whoever wishes may return to what al-Bāqillānī said when discussing the places of eloquence in this sūra.

safi-cedvel:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (علما) second direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative (الواو) a conjunction (لله) attached to an omitted predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ) الحمد (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of the name of Majesty (اللفظ الجلالة) (على كثير) attached to (فضّلنا), (من عباده) attached to an adjective of كثير.
Clause: «the implied oath …» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «آتينا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
Clause: «قالا …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, that is: "so they acted upon what We had given them and said: Praise be to Allah …"
Clause: «الحمد لله …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «فضّلنا …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
(16) (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (أيّها) a vocative, a specified indefinite noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative «[Note: and (ها) is for attention (tanbīh) and has no grammatical position.]», (الناس) a badal (substitute) for أيّ - or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) - nominative in form (منطق) second direct object, accusative «[Note: the first object became the deputy agent of (علمنا).]» (من كلّ) attached to (أوتينا), (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (المبين) an adjective of الفضل, nominative.
Clause: «ورث سليمان …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ورث.
Clause: «the vocative and its response:» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «علّمنا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «أوتينا …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
Clause: «إنّ هذا لهو الفضل …» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
Clause: «هو الفضل …» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate (khabar) of إنّ.
(17) (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (لسليمان) attached to (حشر), (جنوده) deputy agent, nominative (من الجنّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of جنوده (الفاء) a conjunction, and the wāw in (يوزعون) is the deputy agent.
Clause: «حشر … جنوده» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال …
Clause: «هم يوزعون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حشر …
Clause: «يوزعون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(18) (حتى) a particle of commencement (على واد) attached to (أتوا), and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness (يا أيّها النمل) like يا أيّها الناس (لا) a negation «[Note: the verb after it came with the emphatic nūn, by analogy in form with the prohibitive lā.]», (يحطمنّكم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative, and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (circumstance) (لا) a negation.
Clause: «أتوا …» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
Clause: «قالت نملة …» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «the vocative and its response …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «ادخلوا …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا يحطمنّكم سليمان» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
Clause: «هم لا يشعرون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
Clause: «لا يشعرون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(19) (الفاء) a conjunction (ضاحكا) a ḥāl of the agent of تبسّم, confirming the content of the verb «[Note: or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because smiling is the beginning of laughter.]», (من قولها) attached to (ضاحكا) «[Note: or attached to (تبسّم).]» and the nūn in (أوزعني) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) (التي) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, an adjective of نعمتك (عليّ) attached to (أنعمت), and likewise (على والديّ) because it is conjoined to the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أشكر …) is in the position of an accusative, second direct object, its governing word being أوزعني.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أعمل …) is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
(برحمتك) attached to a ḥāl of the object of أدخلني, that is: "clothed in Your mercy" (في عبادك) attached to (أدخلني).
Clause: «تبسّم …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قالت نملة.
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تبسّم.
Clause of the vocative and its response … is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech «[Note: it is permissible for the vocative clause to be a parenthetical clause of supplication, with the clause أوزعني being the quoted speech.]».
Clause: «أوزعني …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «أشكر …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «أنعمت …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
Clause: «اعمل» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «ترضاه …» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (صالحا).
Clause: «أدخلني …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوزعني.
(20) (الواو) a conjunction (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a subject (mubtadaʾ) (لي).
attached to an omitted predicate of the subject (ما), (لا) a negation (أم) it is the detached (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل (من الغائبين) attached to an omitted predicate of كان.
Clause: «تفقد …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال «[Note: or it is resumptive, in the course of the story of Solomon, peace be upon him.]».
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تفقّد.
Clause: «ما لي …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لا أرى …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the yāʾ in (لي).
Clause: «كان من الغائبين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(21) (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath, in all three places (أعذّبنه) like يحطمنّكم, and likewise (أذبحنّه, يأتينيّ), (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) (أو) a conjunction in both places (بسلطان) attached to (يأتينّي) «[Note: or to a ḥāl of the agent of يأتيني, that is: "bringing clear authority".]».
Clause: «أعذّبنّه …» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.
Clause: «أذبحنّه …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أعذّبنّه.
Clause: «يأتيني …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أعذّبنّه «[Note: the conjunction here is required by the art of i'rab; as for the meaning, the (أو) before it means إلّا, that is: "I will surely punish him unless he brings me …", or "I will surely slaughter him unless he brings me …"]».
(22) (الفاء) a conjunction (غير) an adverb of time or place «[Note: it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its description, that is: "a stay not long".]», accusative, attached to (مكث), (بما) attached to (أحطت) «[Note: (ما) is a relative or a described indefinite.]», (به) attached to (تحط), (من سبأ) attached to (جئتك), (بنبإ) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جئتك, that is: "bringing news".
Clause: «مكث …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, that is:
"So the hoopoe came and stayed …"
Clause: «قال …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause مكث.
Clause: «أحطت …» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لم تحط به» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما) «[Note: it may be in the position of a genitive, an adjective of the indefinite (ما).]».
Clause: «جئتك …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause أحطت.
(23) (الواو) a conjunction in both places (من كلّ) attached to (أوتيت), (لها) attached to an omitted fronted predicate of the subject عرش.
Clause: «إنّي وجدت …» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «وجدت …» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «تملكهم» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of امرأة.
Clause: «أوتيت …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تملكهم «[Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the agent of تملكهم, with قد implied.]».
Clause: «لها عرش …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تملكهم.
(24) (الواو) a conjunction (قومها) conjoined to the pronoun object in (وجدتها), (للشمس) attached to (يسجدون), (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of الشمس (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (لهم) attached to (زيّن), (الفاء) a conjunction (عن السبيل) attached to (صدّ) (الفاء) a conjunction connecting the effect with the cause (لا) a negation.
Clause: «وجدتها …» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech.
Clause: «يسجدون …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the object of وجدت and what is conjoined to it.
Clause: «زيّن لهم الشيطان …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl «[Note: it may be resumptive within the scope of the quoted speech.]».
Clause: «صدهم …» is conjoined to the clause زيّن …, in the position of an accusative.
Clause: «هم لا يهتدون» is conjoined to the clause صدّهم …, in the position of an accusative.
Clause: «لا يهتدون» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (هم).
(25) (ألّا) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, and the negating lā «[Note: or it is redundant, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an implied (إلى), attached to (يهتدون), that is: "they are not guided to prostration".]» (لله) attached to (يسجدوا), (الذي) a relative in the position of a genitive, an adjective of the name of Majesty (في السموات) attached to الخبء because it has the sense of المخبّأ (the hidden) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl of it, if it is a name for the inanimate things that are hidden.]»
… (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, a direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يسجدوا) is in the position of an accusative, a badal (substitute) for أعمالهم, that is: "Satan made the non-prostration seem fair to them …", and what lies between the badal and the substituted word is a parenthetical.
Clause: «يسجدوا …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «يخرج …» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
Clause: «يعلم …» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يخرج.
Clause: «تخفون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted «[Note: it may be the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما), with no ʿāʾid to be implied.]».
Clause: «تعلنون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (ما), and the ʿāʾid is omitted.
(26) (إلّا) a particle of exception (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in the implied predicate موجود (ربّ) a badal for the detached pronoun, nominative «[Note: or هو is a second predicate of the subject (الله).]».
Clause: «الله لا إله إلّا هو …» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the hoopoe's speech.
Clause: «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (الله).

* Morphology:
(16) منطق: a noun for every utterance by which one expresses what is in the mind; its wazn is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(18) النمل: a generic noun (ism jins) for the well-known animal; its singular is نملة; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(19) ضاحكا: an active participle from the triliteral (ضحك); its wazn is فاعل.
(20) الهدهد: a generic noun for the well-known bird; its singular is هدهدة with ḍamma on both hāʾs and between them a dāl with sukūn, and (also) هدهدة with ḍamma, then kasra, then fatḥa, and هداهدة with ḍamma on the first hāʾ and kasra on the second hāʾ; the plural is هداهد on the pattern of عساكر, and هداهيد on the pattern of مفاتيح; the wazn of الهدهد is فعلل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the lām and sukūn on the ʿayn, and it is also valid with ḍamma, then fatḥa, then kasra..
(22) سبأ: a proper noun for a land in the region of Yemen; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(25) الخبء: a maṣdar of خبأ يخبأ (of the fatḥ class); in the verse the object (maf'ūl) is intended by it … or it is a name for what is hidden in earth or heaven.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in the saying of the Exalted وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً.
Partitiveness and diminution come from indefiniteness, and just as it comes to belittle the thing made indefinite, so it comes also to magnify it. The apparent sense of His saying «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً», in the context of conferring favour, is a magnification of the knowledge they were given, as if He had said: "knowledge, and what knowledge!" And so it is, for their knowledge was of the kind that is deemed great and astonishing, among it the knowledge of the speech of birds and all the animals, which Allah the Exalted singled them out with; and all knowledge, relative to the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, is little and slight.
2- The use of a preposition: in the saying of the Exalted حَتَّى إِذا أَتَوْا عَلى وادِ النَّمْلِ.
He made أتوا transitive with على because the coming was from above, so he used the preposition of elevation. Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī gazed at this lofty sky and said:
فلشد ما جاوزت قدرك صاعدا ... ولشدّ ما قربت عليك الأنجم
(How greatly you have surpassed your station in ascending, and how greatly the stars have drawn near to you.)
And he said «عليك», not «إليك», because the nearness of the stars is from the direction of height.
3- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the saying of the Exalted قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ.
It is as if, when she saw them heading for the valley, she fled from them for fear of destruction, and another followed her, and she cried out a cry by which she alerted the ants around her, and they followed her. This was likened to the addressing and advising of rational beings, and for that reason they were treated as such, since she was made the speaker and the rest of the ants the ones addressed; so the speech comes out in the form of a representative metaphor, and it is permissible that it be an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya).
4- Jinās al-taṣrīf (paronomasia of inflection): in the saying of the Exalted وَجِئْتُكَ مِنْ سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ:
Jinās al-taṣrīf is the difference in form between two words through the substitution of one letter for another, either from the same point of articulation or one close to it. It is among the beauties of speech connected with the wording, on condition that it comes naturally, or is fashioned by one who knows the essence of speech, preserving with it the soundness and rightness of the meaning. Here it has come with more than soundness, and so it is beautiful, and is novel in wording and meaning. Do you not see that had «بخبر» been put in place of «بنبإ» the meaning would have been sound, yet as it has come it is sounder, because of the added sense in النبأ (news of weight) which corresponds to the description of the situation.

* Benefits:
1- The speech of the birds:
Muqātil said - and I think he took his statement from the Isrāʾīliyyāt: Solomon was sitting in his camp, whose area was a hundred farsakhs by a hundred, twenty-five for the jinn, twenty-five for mankind, twenty-five for the birds and twenty-five for the wild beasts; and the jinn had woven for him a carpet of gold and silk, a farsakh by a farsakh. He saw a nightingale on a tree and said to his companions: "Do you know what this bird says?" They said: "Allah and His Prophet know best." He said: "It says: I have eaten half a fruit, so let the world be effaced." And a hoopoe passed over a tree, and he said: "Seek forgiveness of Allah, you sinners."
And a female bird cried out, and he told them that it was saying: "Would that these creatures had not been created." A peacock cried out, and he said it was saying: "As you judge, so shall you be judged." A swallow cried out, and he said it was saying: "Send forward good, you will find it." A ṭayṭawī cried out, and he said it was saying: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High." And the kite (as he went along) was saying: "Everything will perish except His Face."
The sandgrouse says: "Whoever keeps silent is safe." The parrot says: "Woe to him whose concern is the world." The rooster says: "Remember Allah, you heedless ones." The vulture says: "Son of Adam, live as you wish, your end is death." The eagle says: "In distance from people there is companionship." The frog says: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High …!"
2- A questioner asked: What made Solomon laugh?
The answer came: What made him laugh was two things:
The first: the ant's acknowledgement of his mercy and the mercy of his troops, and her saying وهم لا يشعرون, for had they perceived, they would not have done it.
The second: his delight at what Allah had given him, namely his understanding of the language of the ant, small and humble as she is.
3- The ḥāl is of two kinds:
explanatory (mubayyina) and confirmatory (muʾakkida):
a- The explanatory ḥāl: that whose meaning cannot be gathered without it, such as «جاء خالد راكبا»: the meaning of riding is not gathered except by mentioning the ḥāl «راكبا».
b- The confirmatory: that whose meaning is gathered without mentioning it, and it has several types: we pass over them and refer the reader to the longer books of grammar.
4- Sabaʾ:
It is a land lying in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, in the land of Yemen. It is mentioned in the books of the Old Testament and in the writings of the Arabs and the Greeks, and it is said that it was of great civilisation, and that its people traded in gold, silver and precious stones.
5- Bilqīs: she is the daughter of Sharāḥīl ibn Abī Sarj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Ṣayfī ibn Sabaʾ; and it is said that her father was one of the great kings.
Sabaʾ is the father of the Yemeni tribes that were scattered after the incident of the Maʾrib dam.
6- al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa agreed that the prostrations of the Qur'an are fourteen. They differed over the prostration of Ṣād and the two prostrations of al-Ḥajj.
7- The story of the flood of al-ʿArim:
Among the legends of the Arabs: that Sabaʾ is the father of the Arab tribes scattered because of the Maʾrib dam.
Sabaʾ was among the finest and most fertile of Allah's lands, the richest in trees and water; Allah mentioned that it was two gardens, on the right and on the left, and it was a month's journey for a diligent rider, travelling through gardens from its beginning to its end, with the sun never meeting him nor the shade leaving him, along with flowing water, clear air and wide open space. They remained as long as Allah willed, no king opposing them but they broke him. In the beginning of time floods would overrun their land, so the king of Ḥimyar gathered the people of his kingdom and consulted them about warding off the flood; they agreed to dig channels for it to lead it to the sea. He mobilised the people of his kingdom until he diverted the water, and built a dam at the place where the water flowed down from the mountains, paving it with stones and iron, and made in it conduits for the water of a cubit's circumference; when the flood came, its water was distributed through the conduits to their gardens and crops, by a measure whose benefit reached them all.
